rows.text: But just moments ago, a gray-haired, black-hearted hater slipped into the academy, plotting something dreadful against Sparxicle! I am so scared! You... You won't stand by and let the adorable Sparxicle be hurt, right?
rows.speaker: Broadcast

rows.text: Where could {F#s}he be hiding in the school? Please? Let's root out this villain together!
rows.speaker: Broadcast

rows.text: Of course. This is Planarcadia. Any story can be turned into a comic here.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: ...You are such a curious one. You were fleeing for your life a moment ago, yet now you can talk so casually about such nonsense. Is that really what matters right now?
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: You are hiring a killer? That will not do.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: It doesn't take a rocket scientist to figure out that you can't defeat Sparxie and her rabid fans all by yourself right now.
(Search for the exits)
Open the door! Hiding won't save you! We will drag you out soon enough!
rows.speaker: Voice from Outside

rows.text: As expected, Sparxie's been plotting this for a while. She won't leave you even the slightest chance of escape.
Outside the door, hurried and chaotic footsteps gradually approached.
You want to escape? The match has not even begun, and you have already lost your initiative. The enemy had both taken your qualification to join and your friends.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: I don't like it when someone answers my question with another question. Think before you speak.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: A poster, jarringly out of place, has appeared on the archive room's blackboard. You swear you hadn't seen it the last time you were here.
That resolve is interesting. There will always be foolhardy Supplicants donning the mask in these ancient Phantasmoon Games, laying before the Phantasmoon their madness, fancies, and humor...
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: ...a pink-furred fox?
Then it is done.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: The one in the class photo...?
Gray Hair... Are you all right?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Can't say I am surprised. It sounds exactly like something I would dream of, and something she would carry out the moment she awoke.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Still, it ain't too bad compared to the horrors that unfolded in previous Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Sparxie has taken over a school!
At least you still have friends willing to stand by you, right?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Uh... Now and then I do odd jobs here... livestreaming is one of them. Sparxie is the name I used to stream online. An avatar that I personally sketched line by line.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: To keep the streams running even when I was absent, I breathed a trace of power into that avatar.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Who would've figured that everything changed after the Phantasmoon turned full...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: She's nothing more than a basic skin that's desperate for online attention! Don't compare her with me.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Why are you here?
People offloaded their wishes and desires to her, and in the end, she too got consumed by these emotions.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Once a creation gains a will of its own from the attention of the masses, even its creator can no longer restrain it.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You briefly explained the situation at Graphia Academy.
You want to tell her that these few hours felt like some absurd dream, but the strange paper mask beside you proves that everything was real.
I've been watching you from the start, waiting for the right moment to step in and help. Sadly, you were either with the IPC's people or with the Department of Aberration Defense.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Then you and darling March wandered right into that school of bad omens. That was when I realized things had slipped out of my hands.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: So, tell me, what happened in that school?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: (Is this the mask of Elation that grants entry into the Phantasmoon Games?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What should we do next?
I would.
I won't.
What do you think? Call your companions on the Express ASAP. Or, since this is a civilized society, you could try phoning the Security Bureau.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: But these matters are obviously far beyond what they can do. They say that no one could restrain the Supplicants' actions in the past. Aww, those were the good ol' days of freedom.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Hahaha, Gray Hair, you are so naive! You've been to countless worlds. When the skies collapse and the end draws near, what can the authorities possibly do? Don't make their jobs too hard.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The Phantasmoon Games are nothing less than a ceremony set down by the Master of Elation. Amazing miracles always appear in the world after every game ends, like the birth of new imagenae, unthinkable phenomena, or a future brimming with hope.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Perhaps you have heard the question: "If the world's science and technology could leap forward by a hundred years at the cost of a single kitten's life, would you kill the kitten?"
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Wow, how ruthless. Then you chose the same answer as this world did.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Heh... But clearly, Planarcadia would.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: And this girl summed you up perfectly with just one word: "protagonist". No doubt about it, she's a genius!

Natural disasters, traffic accidents, sudden illnesses... the number of deaths from such causes in this world could fill a small city every day. The Phantasmoon Games are just erasing one school from the map. Isn't that much better?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You're young, {F#beautiful}{M#handsome}, and incredibly talented, but most importantly, you possess the noble quality of being humble and low-key. You're about to tell this girl loudly that you're not some protagonist, you're—
You probably want to ask whether the worth of human lives can truly be calculated in that way in this ceremony, where we surrender that cost to purchase the future.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: No one knows.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Whatever. This is not the time to debate over ethics. Gray Hair, are you gonna save darling March and Mr. Yang or not?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The hour grows late, Miss Pearl. Matters regarding the Express demand our attention...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Be it the alliance or the Phantasmoon Games, if you seek deeper cooperation, my doors remain open.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Then, I shall take my leave.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How intricate human social interaction models are. My extrapolation still cannot account for the full strategy tree of the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Master, General Yao Guang of the Xianzhou Yuque is here to see you. Shall we have her wait?
rows.speaker: Mia

rows.text: No. The Xianzhou will also become a key ally. Only through enough contact and emulation can we hope to comprehend their methods and strategies.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Conclusion: I don't think I'll be able to keep copying the painting for the rest of today. Let General Yao Guang in.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: I am the honorary dean of the Omniscience Sapientia Academe, master of the Deca-Light Reflection Barrier, bearer of the Xianzhou's intangible cultural heritage "the sparrow-shaped fist," and the Seer Strategist— General Yao Guang.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Thank you for seeing me despite your busy schedule, Madam Pearl.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: For a moment, I nearly mistook your words as a fault in language processing: I believed you had brought the entire delegation inside.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Few Intellitrons in the cosmos have a sense of humor. I have heard that, like {RUBY_B#Screwllum}that genius{RUBY_E#}, you are one of the many wonders wrought by the Celestial Differentiator of Planet Screwllum. Meeting you in person far outshines your reputation.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Madam Pearl, seeing how you have a "calculating" look, and with your heart pristine and your outer form so dazzling, I could not help but cast a divination for you. The hexagram lies between Fire and Heaven, demonstrating a bountiful harvest with your fortunes lying at the zenith or even beyond.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I have no training in divination. General, may I ask you to interpret it?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Ah, then let me speak in terms even an Intellitron can follow. I extrapolated your fortune using the Xianzhou's predictive algorithms. The result is 101111, a sign of great blessing. If you treat others with sincerity, abundance will follow.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I have long heard of the Arbiter Generals' legends: the strategy of General Jing Yuan, the courage of General Feixiao, the ingenuity of General Huaiyan...
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Often, I have wondered: what kind of figures are the Xianzhou generals who remain away from the public eye?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Meeting General Yao Guang today, I cannot help but think that: with such beauty, you should step into the light more often.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Looks like you've studied the words of the Xianzhou well. You've even learned the art of "provocation."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You praised the others for their individual and unique talents, yet when it comes to me, the only thing you had to say was "beauty"?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Do not misunderstand me, general. To me, beauty is the rarest of treasures and the most fragile to preserve.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Besides, intel on you is truly scarce. It is quite difficult for me to find ways to compliment you.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: But what I do know is: The Yuque is the think tank of the Xianzhou ships, and its general is the master of all diviners. Speaking purely of deciding the course of affairs, no one is better suited than you to cast the Xianzhou Alliance's vote on whether to join the Anti-Destruction Alliance.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: So, general, what is your decision in this?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: This topic is far too great for me to decide on a whim. But as a gift and to complement the respective gaps in our knowledge, allow me first to offer you a piece of vital intelligence...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: And with it, I ask the IPC to show sincerity beyond empty words.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I do not follow your logic: with the threat of the Destruction looming, what need is there for further reasons to cooperate?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Set a mighty foe as a common goal, convince former enemies to turn allies, then devour them in turn... Such feats are hardly rare in the IPC's annals of glory.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I understand. The Xianzhou questions the IPC's sincerity.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: It would be better to say we ask the IPC to demonstrate its sincerity. Courtesy demands reciprocity, and the intel I now offer you is both urgent and weighty.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Question: what could be more important at this moment than forming the Anti-Destruction Alliance?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Nanook won't erase the universe in the next few days, but someone else might destroy Planarcadia within that time.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You have heard of Blade, the Stellaron Hunter, right?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: The IPC has long placed a great bounty on his head, though I have never laid eyes on him.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: The Yuque recently intercepted a report. Styling himself as "Xianzhou's Number One Assassin," this man accepted a contract from the Synwish Syndicate, a local organized violence group.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I do not know his exact aim here, but he is a major criminal of the Xianzhou. He is guilty of the Ten Unpardonable Sins and is a formidable fighter, with few able to match him. As General of the Yuque, I will take it upon myself to bring him in before he can cause disaster here.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: This planet, Ahatopia, is part of the Pan-Cosmic Trade System, and Blade is a wanted criminal of the IPC. Since he has set foot here, he falls under its law.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: General Yao Guang, by 'sincerity,' do you mean that you wish for us to capture this individual and deliver him to the Xianzhou?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: I hear the Phantasmoon Games are about to begin, with the entire nation awaiting it with bated breath. I imagine you will also find it hard to extract yourself from the festivities. If this cursed man were to quietly "depart on his own" at this time... would that not be a perfect outcome for all?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: This is my understanding: you wish for the right to act freely within Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Apart from this cooperation, what better proof of sincerity could there be before we join forces against the Destruction?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Deal. What I do not doubt: the might of an Arbiter General. However, I do doubt: will "the Xianzhou's Number One Assassin" truly "leave" without a commotion?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: By my extrapolations, even without accounting for the guidance of Destiny's Slave, the probability of capturing a single Stellaron Hunter is less than 9.8 percent.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Not even ten percent? As a diviner, that's not how I see probability.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Even if the chance of success is only a coin toss, once I enter the fray myself... I always treat it as a "one-hundred-percent certainty."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: The Synwish Syndicate... is like the most disgusting filth staining the beautiful Dovebrook River.
rows.speaker: Blissfully Happy Lady

rows.text: Yeah. If only we could make them all disappear. "Happiness and laughter~ starting today!"
rows.speaker: Happy Magic Wand

rows.text: Is that even a question? "One hundred percent," of course.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: In other words, there will be... no survivors.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Anyone who recognizes my face... I will not let them off even if they hide at the ends of the world.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That spear of his looks seriously deadly.
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Don't make eye contact with him...
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: It'll poke a thousand holes right through you!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: This is the Xianzhou's Number One Assassin?
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: So terrifying, so terrifying...
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Everyone, look sharp! Don't let me down!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: How come there's someone who doesn't look like they're from the Xianzhou?
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Shh, don't ask questions. You got a death wish or something?
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: I was willing to make an exception when I was hired by your gang's leader, but I see you folks are not interested in accepting my good will.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Not that I don't trust you, but you know the rules of the trade.
rows.speaker: Ferocious Ploo in a Suit

rows.text: When you hire someone to do a job, you gotta see what they're made of first.
rows.speaker: Ferocious Ploo in a Suit

rows.text: People say that the lords of hell are easy to deal with, but their underlings are the real trouble. If a group's underlings don't know their place, even their masters may not be safe.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: So, since the mighty Synwish Syndicate gang actually had the guts to hire the Xianzhou's Number One Assassin...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I guess you are also ready for "destruction."
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: (Years of wandering have given me nothing but exhaustion, and I have finally come to know how harsh the road of life truly is...)
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ("Impersonating the Xianzhou's Number One Assassin"... Madam Yao, you really stuck me with a "wonderful task.")
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Not long ago...
Please take great care during this mission, Miss Tingyun. If any misfortune should befall you, I would have no way to answer to your Helm Master Yukong.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You worry too much, Madam Yao. When I pledged my resolve to Madam Yukong and departed for the Yuque, I had already steeled myself for the worst.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But... may I ask: Does this task of "misfortune" really have to fall upon me?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I cast a divination today. This task lacks the fire element. Without the Whistling Flames Amicassador's knack for diplomacy, this task cannot succeed.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: The place you're heading to is crawling with gang members. If they pick a fight, you can try to drop the name "Xianzhou's Number One Assassin" and they might step aside.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Do not worry, general. I have journeyed far and wide with the merchant guilds for years and faced no shortage of danger. A handful of gangsters is hardly difficult to deal with.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If you're not afraid of danger, then why have you not set out yet? Shall I read your fortune and give you a little peace of mind?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: What I fear is that "fortune-telling" of yours... No, what I really fear is you, Madam Yao.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Afraid of me? Am I so notorious on the Xianzhou Luofu?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I've heard many tales about you. After the Battle of the Fanghu, you willingly surrendered your command token and became a "general in name only," with neither troops nor soldiers. They also say...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That the Seer Strategist, for the sake of a tiny chance at victory, stood by as {RUBY_B#the Yuque Master Diviner}her mentor{RUBY_E#} went to a noble death, treated the countless lives of dead Verdant Knights as nothing more than numbers consumed in her divinations, and even "doomed" an {RUBY_B#Yueyu}Arbiter-General{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Are you afraid that I, the "cold-blooded diviner," might send you to your "doom" here in Planarcadia? Bold words for a little fox!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: It's just a bit of my curiosity about you, general. I hoped you could clear up a few of my doubts.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Hahaha, seems like I wasn't wrong about you. Few can face a Xianzhou general with such composure and dignity.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: No wonder you could make such a bold statement: "The gods use humans as pawns in their cosmic game, sacrificing countless innocent souls... Have you ever thought about making THEM pay?"
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: They say you survived a Lord Ravager's deadly clutches thanks to luck, but I believe it was your unbreakable resilience that carried you through.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You flatter me, Madam Yao. One must glean some wisdom to be worthy of enduring such a life-and-death ordeal.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If we surpass the gods only in cruelty and heartlessness, then that would be our complete failure in my eyes.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...Excellent, I couldn't agree more! Miss Tingyun, you've passed the interview.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Ever since I escaped death, I swore never again to be a pawn for heartless chess players. And Madam Yao, you've passed my test, too.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I know you're not interested in empty talk, so let's get down to business. Miss Tingyun, our Yuque business delegations are treated much better than what you get on the Luofu when they set out on official missions! They get five meals a day...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: General, I really don't have such a large appetite.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: For the duration of the delegation's mission, you'll receive six times the usual allowance, and all expenses will be fully reimbursed.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Such a generous offer? To be honest, that makes me even more nervous...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Head to Dovebrook District, locate the Synwish Syndicate contact, use the passphrase you gave me to establish contact, and do not reveal my true name.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If there's nothing more to it, is this task really worth six times the pay?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You're the kind of talent worthy of such a reward. After all, we diviners are no different from you merchants. Even when we hit a dead end, we still have to bargain and carve out the faintest chance.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Merchants strive for profitable opportunities, while diviners reach for a sliver of luck.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Looks like my mission bears significant weight in Madam Yao's reading of fate. In that case, I shall depart.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: When in doubt, open the three strategy pouches I entrusted to you. Inside are tactics I divined, certain to break any deadlock and aid your journey.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Go, "Xianzhou's Number One Assassin."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: (Time to get down to business. Where could the Synwish Syndicate be hiding?)
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: (The contact from the Syndicate should stand out.)
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Those people over there... are they also members of the Synwish Syndicate?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's the Synwish Syndicate headquarters across the river. Quite impressive, don't you think?
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Please follow me.
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Is this... the passage in the painting?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: All of you, shut up!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Of course. The Synwish Syndicate has it under our command for now!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Lady Terror in Fog, what do you say? I can find you a few sparring partners. No need to hold back.
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Underboss, you are back. Thanks for your hard work!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Members

rows.text: Who's this fox?
rows.speaker: Confused Member

rows.text: Welcome home, Underboss!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Members

rows.text: Is this the one the boss brought in?
rows.speaker: Confused Member

rows.text: Underboss, I mean no disrespect, but... is this frail woman really the one the boss invited!?
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: That's right! Her name is The Terror in Fog. Spread the word that the Synwish Syndicate has secured Xianzhou's Number One Assassin!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Underboss, beat me if you want, but I gotta say... Are you serious? Are we really counting on this delicate woman for the Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Oh no. These brutes are not interested in a win–win situation at all...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: "When in doubt, open the three strategy pouches I entrusted to you. Inside are tactics I divined, certain to break any deadlock and aid your journey."
Looks like it's time...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: (The Phantasmoon Games... Is that why they hired a Stellaron Hunter to do their bidding?)
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: These Phantasmoon Games are a once-in-a-lifetime chance for the Synwish Syndicate to rise! This woman doesn't look like she has what it takes, and we're trusting her? If she blows it, how are we supposed to save face?
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Underboss! We haven't been duped, have we? If word gets out, the other gangs will laugh us out of town...
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Useless! Lady Terror in Fog would wipe the floor with you even if you all came at once. Since you doubt her, why not let Lady Terror in Fog show you a few moves?
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: I thought you were naive, but looks like you're just playing good cop, bad cop to test me?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Nah, I'm neither good nor bad... just opportunistic.
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Still playing dumb, huh...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Boss of the Synwish Syndicate, your people wouldn't be doing this on their own. I know you can hear me...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I came for business. Making friends would be a fine bonus, but if not, that's fine with me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If you still want this deal, cut the tricks.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: A real expert is something else. You speak with such overwhelming presence... though we barely understand a word. Come on, show us a move. We fight and bleed every day, and that's the only way we'll be convinced.
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Huh...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: "Just keep... alive, and open the second strategy pouch once you're done. (^O^)/"
rows.speaker: Yao Guang's Strategy Pouch

rows.text: (What kind of strategy is this? There's barely anything helpful in here.)
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Looks like Lady Terror in Fog isn't impressed with your skills. Outta my way!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: When I was young, I dreamed of becoming a musician. But fate had other plans, and I was dragged into a world of violence.
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: But even then, I never let go of my love for music and rhythm. Even in battle, I kept honing my singing and instrumental skills!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: And that's how I forged my one-of-a-kind fighting style. They call me... the Roaring Caustide!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Oh cribs! The Underboss... is getting serious!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Lady Terror in Fog, I humbly challenge you! Show the Synwish Syndicate the assassination skills you're so proud of!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Underboss! Bad news! Two more weird dudes just showed up!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Cut your bull. I can see for myself!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Never thought visiting an ally would mean crashing into a local gang's hall.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ah, this will take some explaining...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: What a twist of fate... but for us to reunite with an old friend here... so be it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You two, stand down! Listen well! This will be an honorable duel!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: A duel? You dare duel a Xianzh—
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...a Xianzhou's Number One Assassin, and you still dare to act so brazen?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Come on, Madam, it's pointless to say anything now.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Wait, "a"? What do you mean, "a" Xianzhou's Number One Assassin? Who exactly are you!?
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: Even a cunning hare keeps three burrows. Who ever told you... there was only one "Xianzhou's Number One Assassin"?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: So... there are three of you?
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: No! It's three hundred! Times have changed. The title "Xianzhou's Number One Assassin" is already a brand. At my side stands...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The organization's seventh-ranked Halovian Reaper, the "Winged Deathknell"! He sends every target into the sweetest sleep of death.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: And this one is the second-ranked assassin in the organization, a ruthless killer surpassed only by me! His spear strikes like a falling star, and his presence soars like a dragon. They call him the "Jadedragon"!
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Then you are...?
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: You can call me "Whistling Flamefox." I humbly hold the top position in our organization, though I mostly handle business relations and HR work.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Hard to believe, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If you want this gentleman to know you speak the truth, let {RUBY_B#Dan Heng}our brother{RUBY_E#} show off a bit of his spear work. That will convince them.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hahaha, I say there's no need for that!
Caustide, you insisted on testing them and got nothing out of it, did you? If you had let them meet me sooner, none of this would have happened.
Boss! I cannot hand your grand enterprise over to people we know nothing about!
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: You are the one who hired us? The boss of the Synwish Syndicate?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's me. I am Polwave, current leader of the Synwish Syndicate. My apologies. Our gang is full of roughnecks. I will make sure they are disciplined.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: As for "that business," we'll discuss it upstairs. Everyone else, clear out!
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: I gotta say, this place is decorated with a touch of style.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: A gang does not always flaunt brute force. More often, they need to flaunt wealth.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Before I even realized, the scenery of Dovebrook became unrecognizable.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: Back then, who would have imagined {RUBY_B#mechatrons}iron hulks{RUBY_E#} running wild on the streets, let alone us gang members being treated like vermin?
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: You didn't call us here just to reminisce, did you?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Haha, of course not! Please forgive Caustide's rude little test.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: That narrow-minded fellow never understands why young people flock to things that come from other planets, like mechatrons, masked heroes, and the Astral Express...
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: What he does not see is that while cosmic novelties are more enticing, big shots that hail from the cosmos are even more fearsome.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: Wouldn't you agree?
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: You're a clever one, so there's no point in keeping up this charade. We're not "Xianzhou's Number One Assassins." You knew that already, didn't you?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I may not live as long as those Xianzhou folks, but I've got a decent eye for sizing people up. You might not be the number one assassins, but your skills surpass even such assassins.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: So I don't care who you are. I paid good money for a "sharp blade"...but I don't give a fig about its brand.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: And where do you intend to use this blade?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: On the Synwish Syndicate.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: What?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Don't get me wrong. I am not looking for bloodshed. Instead, I intend to perform surgery on the Synwish Syndicate. Look here...
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: Through certain connections, I secured this "Mask of Elation," the entry pass to the Aeonic game. Some covet this treasure, while others fear it a curse.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: Now, you claimed the name of "Xianzhou's Number One Assassins," so surely you came for this. You want the god's reward, don't you?
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: You are our employer. Therefore, the festival's prize should rightfully be yours. What do you want from the Aeon, Mr. Polwave?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Aeon? I harbor no such unrealistic desire.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: I'll leave this prize for you to claim as your reward. I'm happy enough to share in a bit of your glory...
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: Whether you win or lose, all I ask is that when the press comes knocking, you say this: You were sponsored by the Synwish Syndicate of Dovebrook. That is enough for me.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: So this is a sponsorship deal? The Synwish Syndicate only wants fame?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Since we are not truly in your employ, are you not afraid we might break our promise and ignore your request?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If you truly cared nothing for what I asked, why even raise the question? As I said before, I may not have the long life of the Xianzhou people, but I do know how to judge people.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: One more question from me, please. Why are you so set on chasing fame?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: In Planarcadia, imagenae exist due to Wishpower, and that Wishpower comes from the attention, curiosity, and demands humans place upon these imagenae.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: The Synwish Syndicate was founded to provide for those imagenae who were ignored, had no Wishpower, and were not needed by humanity.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: Unfortunately, ever since that {RUBY_B#Pearl}seashell woman{RUBY_E#} rose to power, our path of blood and violence had run its course.
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: That's why I want the Synwish Syndicate to take on a new form, one that will draw more attention than ever before!
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: The Synwish Strangeling Pension Foundation. What do you think of the name?
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: ...It's a cozy and heartwarming name.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hahaha! So, will the three of you accept this job?
rows.speaker: Boss Polwave

rows.text: Umm... sorry, Sunday. My body instinctively sensed danger.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "Once the mask for joining the Phantasmoon Games is worn, it binds tightly to the Supplicant and manifests the shape of the wearer's soul." I read something like this in the Views of the Universe from a Starskiff.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: It's confirmed now. This mask is indeed genuine.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Congratulations, Mr. Sunday. You're now a Supplicant in the Aeonic game.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: What exactly are you trying to do, Seer Strategist? Twice now you've acted without warning. Do you mean to make an enemy out of the Astral Express?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Dan Heng.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Let me take care of this.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: (Sunday... are you planning to fight?)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Don't worry. I'm no match for this general.)
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: General Yao Guang... How'd you pierce my thoughts? I ran a check with my "tuning," and there were no signs of any outside intrusion.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: They say a diviner can't read hearts. I call that the excuse of mediocrity. Mr. Sunday, you're fascinated by the Phantasmoon Games. You even wondered "what if I wore this mask," didn't you?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You can even divine thoughts like that?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: No. I'm simply good at seeing using my "eyes." Though Mr. Sunday never asked to examine the mask, he's glanced at it at least three times since we started the conversation.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Given the character and manners of someone as noble as him, I can't think of any motive for this action but "genuine interest."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: ...Sunday?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yes. I did think of it. For a moment, I even considered putting it on.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So I merely gave you what you desired. This is no trap. It's just an unexpected "gift"...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: During the Phantasmoon Games, I'll give every ounce of aid I can to help you seize your chance to have an audience with the Aeon.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: General Yao Guang... As far as I know, throwing out heavy profits first is usually a lure to make others lose.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: We've only just met. I don't understand why you'd go this far?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Why belittle yourself? Every move I've made is to carve a sliver of "possibility" from "the impossible."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: With my Eye of Īśvara, I see you're the only one in this land who doesn't need to do a thing for me. Simply acting on your own will can bring change.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: "Your own will"...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Indeed. Dan Heng, I do want to learn more about this world.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Because this world of Elation fascinates me. Is Planarcadia... truly a paradise? An arcadia that its name claims?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I once pursued a mistaken vision of paradise with stubborn resolve. Even now, I can't say for sure what a true paradise should look like.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That's why I want to see with my own eyes whether this "arcadia" lives up to its name.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So then, as long as Mr. Sunday acts, that "omen of death" Madam Yao foresaw...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Of course it would still come to pass! Did you think just a lavish gift could let you stroll out of destiny's shackles alive?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Pardon me for butting in... But does the Xianzhou know about this?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: This is such serious business. I'd never make this decision on my own. I've talked it over with the Six Charioteers of the Yuque. If something happens to me, I'll line up a solid successor.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: She headed to the Yuque on the day I left on this mission, just in case anything went wrong. There, with the other potential successors picked by the Six Charioteers, she'll train at the Omniscience Sapientia Academe in divination arts, war strategies, and civil governance.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You mean Lady Fu Xuan? She'd take over the Yuque after you?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Fu Xuan? What Fu Xuan?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: If I don't make it back from this trip, maybe Qingque from the Luofu Divination Commission could take the Seer Strategist's position and command the Yuque...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: ...Qingque and Yuque. What a perfectly rhymed match!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: As for the details... shall we discuss this somewhere else, you three?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: This way please, Miss Hacker.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Sorry, but you will have to take a "side path." The landlord of this magazine office fled to dodge his debts, and creditors have been storming in one after another. In the end, Mr. Detective sealed the front door entirely.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Map says the "Ashen Detective Agency" should be right here.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Some time later, in search of stolen items, an uninvited guest quietly slipped into Dovebrook District.
...But why's there just a magazine publisher's office?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Holy furboly! Heard big drama hit Graphia Academy!
rows.speaker: Furbobocom Reporter

rows.text: A furbo? Taking photos? You really can find anything in the land blessed by Aha. Let's go ask for directions.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: So this is where the detective lives?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Yes, his office and living quarters are one and the same. It is a little shabby, I admit. At this hour... he is probably fast asleep. Visitors here are rare indeed.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Visitors being rare... that really does sound a little sad.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Please, come with me. I will wake him at once.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Let's get down to business. I can stroll around later.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Mr. Ashveil, this lady is not here for food delivery.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Oh, then she must be here to kill me?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Sadly, not that either.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: What do you mean, "sadly"...?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Not here to deliver food, AND not here to kill me. How strange... Oh! Then you must be a client! You are here to hire me for a case!
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Your order of guesses is a little heartbreaking. Yes, I am here to commission you. Something has been stolen.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Oh? What did you lose?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: A person, along with an ancient mask that should have been mine.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Heh, interesting. Are you here to join the Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: At that moment, a cloud of suspicion rises in the detective's mind. Who exactly is this girl?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Mister N, stop the voiceover when we're talking business.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Huh? Stop? You pay me nine hundred credits an hour plus two bananas just for this, don't you?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Yes, but at least throw me a few clues while you work. Between a detective and their assistant, at least one of them should know a thing or two about deduction, right?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: A name flashed through the otherwise empty mind of the detective. This unremarkable-looking girl was in fact one of the top ten most wanted terrorists on the IPC's bounty list, a Stellaron Hunter...
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: ...Kafka!
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: It's Silver Wolf! She's Silver Wolf! Mr. Ashveil, did you get your head caught in the fridge door or something?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: I feel like I need to wipe my personal data again.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: One of the Interastral Peace Corporation's most wanted fugitives with the highest bounties, comes to commission a broke detective... I have seen plenty of stories like this.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: So, the next thing would be me getting dragged into a massive conspiracy and forced to run for my life, right?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Drop the paranoia. I came to you because I hacked into the Security Bureau's criminal records system.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: What I found was shocking. In all those bizarre police cases, you were hired again and again.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: "The Curious Case of the Harmony Sect Communion," "The Mystery of the Ghost Bullet Wyrm Express," "The Serial Ghost Resurrection Incident," "The Super-Non-Serial Locked-Room Murders at Kooky House"... you helped solve them all.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You may not be the most famous, but you're probably the most capable detective around here, right?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Is nothing private anymore... Whatever. Tell me, how did you lose your mask?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Today was supposed to be our meeting with the Synwish Syndicate...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Alright, now let's talk about the commission fee.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Excuse me? I haven't even finished my sentence yet...?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: A true great detective can know a case without ever leaving the room.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: While he sleeps, I gather the intel. We already have the basics about today's fiasco with the Synwish Syndicate, and those three "Xianzhou's Number One Assassins" who scammed the mask.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Can you handle it? Money is not a problem. Do you take dirty money?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Sorry, no dirty money. And please do not withdraw your payment plus the account balance after paying.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Oh, then how about this? This is the IPC's turf, right? Turn me in for the bounty.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You take the reward, and I bolt afterward. We Stellaron Hunters sometimes use that trick to raise funds.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...Or maybe we could discuss the possibility of taking dirty money. Thirty million credits. Pay us after the work's done.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Deal. I'll try to get that money over the next few days. Here's my contact info. Update me the moment you have any news.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Pay us after the work? When did our office have a rule like that?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: That rule got made just now. Oh, my dear Mister N, did you truly want to take dirty money? I have come up with another way to make money. Let me reach out to a certain big shot first.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Madam Pearl, I've obtained solid intel!
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: ...Mr. Ashveil? The chance of you initiating a call at this hour is under five percent.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Let me guess: Perhaps you are finally ready to consider my offer?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: No, I've found the trail of the Stellaron Hunters! They are here in Planarcadia, and they even plan to crash the Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I can send you her coordinates quietly, without anyone noticing...
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Hmph. Quietly, without anyone noticing.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: The Phantasmoon Games... The moment your IPC chose to speedrun it, it was fated to be more than just a game of fun. And you want me to take part? That is asking a bit much of an old man.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: We should've taken that hacker's deal earlier and turned her in for the bounty.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: An unexpected bonus. So Pearl still has other masks hidden away... That makes things much easier.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Seems that listening in on one's partners after wrapping up business is a habit worth keeping.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Hey Bladie, where are you?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Did you find the mask?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Not yet. But I've got a new lead. We might've lost one mask, so I just need to find another.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Fine. Promise me this: Next time, don't take contracts on the dark web using names like "Xianzhou's Number One Assassin."
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Okay, okay. By the way, can you tell me what script Elio gave you this time?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: A completely blank page.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Ah, I get it. So it's just a typical case of the ideogenitive imagenae phenomenon.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Yeah. You could say that according to the old superstition.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Modern science believes that when something receives excessive attention, it would suddenly gain life and becomes an imagenae due to the accumulation of too much Wishpower.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: What kind of modern science is that supposed to be?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Planarcadia's modern science, of course.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Outworld visitors might find this kind of thing strange... but it's not exactly rare around here.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Sorry, sorry, used a bit of jargon there. "Ideogenitive" here means something born of chance and circumstance.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Heading out? Where to? You mean going to Graphia Academy to arrest this illegal imagenae?
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: *sigh* We can't. I just received notice from the Department of Aberration Defense: The first Supplicant of these Phantasmoon Games has revealed herself, and she's none other than Miss Sparxie, the one you mentioned.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Although you're honored guests of the Astral Express, you seem completely unfamiliar with the laws and customs of this world. During the Phantasmoon Games, we do not traditionally interfere with Supplicants' actions. That is their privilege.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: In other words, since she's a Supplicant, we security officers can't do anything unless she causes actual harm.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: ...Spirit of the Sky, Spirit of the Earth...
rows.speaker: Paraprince

rows.text: ...Please, Aha, show me a sign!
rows.speaker: Paraprince

rows.text: Please give us a new company president~
rows.speaker: Paraprince

rows.text: Oh right, the news broadcast is about to start. Care to watch?
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Hello everyone, welcome to Fulwish TV's special news segment, Arcadian Morning Report! I'm your host, Poofy!
rows.speaker: Host on the Left

rows.text: Hi everyone, I'm your host, Snowie!
rows.speaker: Host on the Right

rows.text: We've entered Year 1999 of the Arcadian Calendar. What an exciting time! Just one more year until the new millennium!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Over 500 years ago, a famous prophet made a prediction: "In Year 1999, a terrifying devil will descend from the sky"! Will this prophecy come true? Can Planarcadia safely make it through this crucial year?
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: You say she took a school hostage, but the intel I have says otherwise.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: You idiot! Are you cursing our viewers? They didn't tune in to hear your fearmongering nonsense! Just read the news, and stick to it!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Y—Yes! Incredibly, after just fifteen years, the Phantasmoon is full again, and the time for the Phantasmoon Games is upon us once more. Surely a blessing from the Master of Elation upon this arcadia!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Just now, the first masked Supplicant has appeared!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Wow! Internet-famous streamer Miss Sparxie announced two hours ago that she's donning a mask to become a Supplicant! The Department of Aberration Defense has confirmed the news is authentic!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: As an ideogenitive imagenae, Miss Sparxie's birth wasn't approved by the Department of Aberration Defense, but that hardly matters at this point.
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: What sort of miracle does this livestreamer plan to produce during the Phantasmoon Games? Let's switch over to her stream and see!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: I'd say she needs us more than we need her.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: One person, a thousand faces! A thousand faces, one person! ♥ Who will Sparxicle become today?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: You told Himeko about the whole series of events with the tabloid journalist following you and the compensation claims. Heh heh, looks like destiny wanted you two to meet again, and maybe score you a nice fat paycheck while at it.
March, say hi to the camera!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Sparxie! Don't you dare mess with me! I, March, am not someone you can easily push around!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: My, March seems quite worked up. Is it because she's a bit nervous about her first live interview?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Alright then, now let me interview my colleague, Mr. Yang!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Hello everyone, I'm Welt Yang, a history teacher at Graphia Academy. I'm honored to be selected as this year's "Most Popular Male Teacher," and I will continue to strive to nurture even more outstanding talents!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Boss, you don't like "Furbobo Gossip"? What name would you prefer then?
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: Thank you all for your wholehearted support! Sparxicle will work hard to repay your kindness! ♥
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: In three hours, I'll be hosting a special livestream performance — SparxiCon — alongside our special guests, the legendary Nameless from the Astral Express who have carved countless legends across the cosmos!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Tell your friends, your family... even your enemies! Let's set aside all grudges and meet in the stream to witness the most dazzling sparks light up Planarcadia!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Have you seen shows like that before? You know, where celebrities go somewhere to do everyday jobs, like those reality shows where they trade places with regular people.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Hahaha, so these are the Nameless of the Astral Express?
rows.speaker: Livestream Spectator

rows.text: Right now, you're their only hope...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: ...and that red boss lady of yours. She's here too.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: [Trailblazer], are you alright? Did you get hurt when you ran away?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...So March and Welt are both trapped in Graphia Academy now? And that girl called Sparxie took the mask, too?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No, it's not your fault. I underestimated the complexity of the situation behind these games.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Coming back to my homeland was meant to be a relaxing vacation for everyone, and I also wanted you and March to experience the atmosphere of Elation in this world.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Everyone has options in life. But some options... they can't help you escape your fate.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You mean, you've witnessed the existence of Terminus? But that doesn't mean your life has entered the Finality, does it?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You might be onto something. When it comes to "Aeons," divination often goes haywire and no proper reading can be formed.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Throughout the history of the Phantasmoon Games, there have been many instances of cooperation between Supplicants.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But this time, forces from across the cosmos have turned this into their own high-stakes poker table.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Rather than honoring the Elation, these players are far more eager to savor victory for themselves, itching to knock everyone else out of the game.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Sparxie is one such troublemaker.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's dangerous to rush back to school on courage alone when we don't know what Sparxie "has done" and what she's "planning to do."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: For every Supplicant, there are three key acts that must be completed once the Phantasmoon Games begin: the "roll-call," the "miracle," and the "promotion."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Next, she must strive to make a "miracle" happen: bear the people's wishes and answer with a great feat.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What could be more earth-shattering than defeating a renowned cosmic hero on a battlefield of her own meticulous design?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So here's the question, Sparkle: Based on what you know about this impostor, what's her real agenda for joining the Games? Simply toying with and defeating the Express crew alone won't be enough. What kind of world-shaking "miracle" is she after?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Sure, she's a fake, but she's still a fake of Miss Sparkle. Guessing won't get us far.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: If you ask me... we should check out the tavern. Might find some leads there!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The Masked Fools' headquarters... the "World's End" Tavern.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's right. How could we pull off something this insane without Miss Sparkle's prized collection I've been hoarding all these years?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: That imposter must've known this well. Before this operation, she definitely went to the tavern... using my name.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Most Fools can't tell the difference between me and that imposter, or maybe they just don't care. But if we can find out who "I" talked to and which treasures "I" stole from my collection of items, we'll naturally figure out what that imposter is up to.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: That's a good plan, but I can't let you act alone. Can you take both of us into the tavern?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Since there's still time, I'll head out first. You two can come over when you're ready.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Relax, [Trailblazer]. To step into the Elation's rite, what you need the most is ease.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Don't dance to your enemy's tune. Find your own rhythm.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Meanwhile, [Trailblazer], who escaped from school alone, actually called the police...
...So what you're saying is that this Miss Sparxie, who was originally just a virtual avatar, has now crossed into reality and taken an entire school's staff and students hostage?
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Now it's our turn to set the steps.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It gained sentience of its will?
Dovebrook District... It's been a while since I've been home. Perfect timing. Dan Heng and Sunday have made some new discoveries. I asked them to meet up with us later.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Don't get your hopes up too high.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Looks like this vacation trip has gone right back to our usual "trouble magnet" mode.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A typical case?

Certain historical eras had imagenae popping up non-stop like mushrooms after a shower. Things are different now, but if you're not careful, you might still find characters from popular comics suddenly show up in the flesh.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: Ideogenitive?
These imagenae arise from incidental events. That's quite different from "progenitive imagenae," which reproduce by having artists draw their offspring.
rows.speaker: Security Officer

rows.text: So when are you heading out?
Now this is the kind of vacation the Nameless just has to savor.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A furbo snapped a pic of me on this street without my consent just now...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Fame isn't exactly good news for the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: She took an entire school hostage!
We're almost at Dovebrook District.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: (Quite a bustling district... Is this really where Himeko lived back then?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It's been fifteen years since I've been back... I wonder what's become of these houses now... If they're being rented out, or if they've been sold off already?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Perhaps they've become like the Graphia family: nothing but empty shells of their former glory.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's go. Stay safe on the road.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hmm, this place seems to have changed a lot...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Holy furboly! Great Raccoon, you really came!
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: Which Supplicants will appear in these Phantasmoon Games, and what mind-blowing miracles will they bring to everyone? With permission from the Department of Aberration Defense, we'll be following and reporting on the Phantasmoon Games from start to finish!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: There's a furbo calling out to you. Why don't we go take a look?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How intriguing! Who are they, and where did they come from? Let's take a look!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Rest assured, I haven't forgotten a single thing about the c—c—compensation.
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: (This furbo was actually waiting outside the magazine's office just to make amends...? Furbo absurdo!)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: And you are...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yoohoo! And we're back from the commercial break! A big thank you to Love Insurance® for being the title sponsor of today's Sparxtacular Arcadian Adventures livestream!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Would you mind coming into our magazine office to talk? Let's discuss compensation, shall we?
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: Ta-da! Time for the big reveal! Everyone, follow along with Dean Sparxie of Graphia Academy as we check out how our new transfer student is settling in!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: It looks like the magazine publisher has taken over this entire building...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Strictly speaking... The entire street where this building stands belongs to my family's estate.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I—I'll have you know I'm the disciple of General Jing Yuan of the Luofu and General Huaiyan of the Zhuming! I've undergone rigorous Xianzhou sword training! Others might fear you, but I sure don't!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's said that, in their heyday, the Graphia family owned property all across Planarcadia, but by my generation, very little was left.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: When my journey reaches its end, will anyone in this world be able to inherit anything from me?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I will inherit Himeko's will.
Alright, that wraps up our interview for now! Let me give you all a sneak peek at what's coming up in our next livestream!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Moooom!
Sorry, I made things a bit too heavy there.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Silly child. What nonsense are you talking about.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Come, let's go inside the magazine office and see what this little furbo is up to.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Great Raccoon, that jerk of a company president ditched everyone to dodge the debts. We brothers haven't gotten paid in months.
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: No way, no way! As your devoted fans, me and my bros sincerely want to compensate you handsomely for your emotional distress!
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: You showed Himeko the strange mask that a young girl drew for you.
I knew you wouldn't pass up an opportunity like this.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I wasn't vigilant enough.

These furbos may be crafty and full of tricks, but they can definitely help us out: A media outlet working for you, and a network of informants who can run around everywhere... Having a logistics team like that during the Phantasmoon Games would come with many perks.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Being a company president is actually super easy, just follow me!
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: Please take a seat in front of the computer, President! I'll show you how it works~
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: Chatting about the Phantasmoon Games together? Cool name!
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: My heart just skipped a beat... but that's okay, as long as the boss is happy!
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: We can't let her get away with this!
Ghost-Ship Grove!? What's that supposed to mean?
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: Sparxie has completed the "roll-call." She took the mask and declared her entry into the games, drawing everyone's attention to the news that "the first Supplicant has appeared."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's quite a unique name!
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: If I'm not mistaken, Sparxie is waiting for us to walk right into her trap. For her, there couldn't be a better opponent than the Astral Express for this first battle between Supplicants...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Are you sure?
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: In return, make sure you create some big news stories!
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: I heard a Supplicant has appeared at Graphia Academy. Should we have him take some pictures there for you?
rows.speaker: Furbulitzer

rows.text: Looks like Dan Heng and Sunday haven't arrived yet. If you're feeling restless, why don't you go outside and explore a bit?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: (Wait until companions arrive)
You mean... your tavern?
(Look around)
What do you think this means, general?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's not as mystical as it sounds. While an īśvara has far greater freedom of choice than ordinary people, they're still caught in the currents of fate. I just want to remind you to choose wisely.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I am not an īśvara free from fate, so naturally I can't guide those of that disposition.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Take this business card. The address of the tavern is printed on it. However, you'll have to find your own way to the tavern. That's been the rule since it was established, and there's nothing I can do about it.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Back to business. I take it you're not just here to read our fortunes?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Can Sparkle... be trusted?
March, Mr. Yang...
I understand Miss Himeko's intentions. [Trailblazer], I'll leave March and Mr. Yang in your care.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Blade's appearance means the Stellaron Hunters are also on the move in this world.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "World's End" Tavern, Location: Dovebrook District, near the Synwish Syndicate Office
From everything we've seen, this mission to Planarcadia is of the utmost importance.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Himeko's home is in Dovebrook District?
I will accompany General Yao Guang to uncover the Stellaron Hunters' schemes. Whatever happens this time, I hope it won't put any of you in danger... I'll do my best to make sure of that.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What... Those two are trapped in the school, forced to "become" a student and teacher? And the security officers are turning a blind eye to all this?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Phantasmoon Games... What a bizarre ceremony. What does this type of Elation really mean for the people of this place? Why would Aha promote such a game?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Whatever happens, keep me posted on how things go.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Greetings, benefactor. It's been many days since we met in Penacony, and I've been thinking of you day and night.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Tingyun... it's been a while.
How are things these days?
The tabloid journalist who took my picture.
Thank you for your concern. I'm doing well.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Though my skills are meager, Madam Yao praised my resolve to kill my enemies, saying that was just the "variable" she sought. That's why she assigned me to temporarily serve under her command for this expedition. And look at that... it's brought us back together again!
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Could it be...
What kind of person is Madam Yao?
How is Madam Yao treating you?
I'll drop by to see you when I get the chance!

Hard to say. Like the divinations she casts, she's a riddle shrouded in fog. Apart from the ever-absent {RUBY_B#Youwu}Patina Justice{RUBY_E#}, she's likely the most mysterious of the Arbiter Generals.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I'm sure there's no mortal danger, teehee... Please forgive my jest, benefactor. Being around Madam Yao has gotten me into the habit of cracking jokes all the time.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: About Blade...

Her actions may seem inscrutable, but she always provides what you need ahead of time. That's why even those who grumble still carry out her orders with diligence. In truth, doesn't she seem more like a shrewd merchant than a diviner?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But then, when have any Arbiter Generals ever been ordinary?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: About March and Welt...
Though March and Mr. Yang don't seem in mortal danger for now, who knows what Sparxie is plotting. The longer we delay, the worse it could get... Better to rescue them as soon as possible.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Don't go back on your word, benefactor! We can find a local bar and share a drink while we chat.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Don't worry. I'm here with you.
Madam Yao instructed me to meet her at our agreed spot if she disappears. It's growing late, so I'll take my leave now.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...A mask of elation can reflect the shape of one's soul?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Sunny, can I take a look at your mask?
What fortune! I wished I could travel with you longer back in Penacony, benefactor. After all, I've yet to reclaim the opportunities Phantylia stole from me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Sure.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: In Penacony's decorative arts, ravens often symbolize the hidden desires and whispers of humans' dreamscapes.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Don't worry, I once tried to ascend to godhood myself... I won't be dazzled by the honor of an audience with a deity.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hmm? There's no rule saying that Supplicants of the Phantasmoon Games have to fight each other, right?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: On the contrary, for the Elation, shouldn't laughter be a resonance that comes from within each other's hearts?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: After putting it on, I seemed to hear... curious voices.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Haha, that's a good one!
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Some came for the alliance, some for the Aeon's game... Whatever their reasons, a storm is brewing in the skies over this world.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: When that General Yao Guang shows up again, I should discuss our collaboration plans with her. Good luck, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The IPC, Masked Fools, a Xianzhou general, the Stellaron Hunters, and the Nameless...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But at least we got some good news. Sunday has joined the Phantasmoon Games. He can help us in our showdown against Sparxie.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's rendezvous with Sparkle at the tavern. We must uncover why Sparxie entered the Phantasmoon Games and what sort of "SparxiCon" she's got planned for Graphia Academy.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Ugh, the Riddlers again?
A long time ago... You scoff to yourself, who even remembers after all this time? But you do remember. When Sparkle first met you, she told you a riddle.
So how do we get into the tavern?

When I was little, I heard a few urban legends. They say the entrance to the tavern exists behind every single door in this land. But those who aren't invited, or haven't found their destined path, can never step inside.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: By watching the sky reflected in water.

This time, we already have the Fools' invitation in hand. As for the key to open the door... there's a silly rhyme on the back of the business card: "For revelry and drinks galore, no need to search from door to door. Heed the Fool's riddle with care, to find the key that leads you there."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So, [Trailblazer], about the Fool's Riddle... got any leads?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Whether they look up or down, the moon that humanity gazes upon in the sky is always the same Phantasmoon.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Don't get too carried away now.
Taking part in this grand event is also about gaining a deeper understanding of this... "arcadia." Just as one cannot miss the Charmony Festival when visiting Penacony.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Will we become enemies?
Looking up makes sense. But looking down... how exactly do you gaze at the sky?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What's the deal with this mask anyway?
The mask whispers to me... urging me to show my "elation" to the god, to create miracles that will make the people of the arcadia laugh with joy.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Now would be the perfect moment!
[Trailblazer], it seems fate ties you to the tavern. I get it now. The answer is Dovebrook.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Many generations ago, the Dovebrook was already a river flowing with countless legends.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's no surprise the door to the tavern lies hidden among them.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Legend has it that the master painter Graphia once drew water from the Dovebrook to wash her paintbrushes.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Many later artists followed suit. Hence, its other name, the "Painters' Stream."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Looking at Dovebrook's scenery... memories from my student days just come flooding back.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko's student days?
Tell me, tell me! I want to hear all about it!
They're not exactly interesting memories. Back then, Dovebrook District was teeming with gangs. There were hooligans running around everywhere, and some really loved messing with the students.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I was taller than my peers and happened to be training in martial arts. To stand up for my juniors, I would occasionally... get into scraps with the thugs on the streets.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The people who fell into the Dovebrook river would cover the surface like bean sprouts in noodle soup... It all feels like it was just yesterday.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko, noodle master!
A thug falling into the water... what a scene!
Sometimes the thugs fell in. Other times, I took the plunge myself.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Back then I was a bundle of restless energy. The teachers always said I was like "a wind-up toy that never stopped banging its drums and cymbals," stirring up a commotion wherever I went.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In the blink of an eye, fifteen years have passed. Hard to believe someone as reckless and willful as me became the Navigator of the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Now's not the time to wax sentimental. We've reached the banks of the Dovebrook, so where's the "tavern" entrance hidden?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "Under Synwish Syndicate requisition"... Looks like we'll have to find another way across.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: According to the business card, the "tavern" is near the Synwish Syndicate headquarters.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's check the other side of the river.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hey folks... have y'all heard the joke about the Dovebrook?
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: Come on, tell us!
One day, a criminal escaped from prison. He ran for his life, but just when freedom seemed within reach, the Dovebrook blocked his path.
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: With his pursuers closing in, the man prayed to the river: "I am hammered by the law, stained with filth. O pure, flowing waters, please do not swallow me."
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: A voice from the Dovebrook replied, "There's a pedestal of light upon the water. Step on it, and you can cross!"
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: The criminal wept: "What pedestal of light? It's only the moon mirrored on the water, an image that shatters at a touch! If I step on it, I'll fall in and drown!"
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: Hahaha, guess how the Dovebrook answered him?
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: Keep your distance from the drunk.
The Dovebrook said, "You're not 'hammered' at all. Otherwise, how could you still tell the moon from a pedestal?" Hahaha... HAHAHA!
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: What are you even talking about?
What are you implying?
That's such a dry joke...
I—It's fine... You don't have to buy me a drink. As long as I can make you laugh! Hahahahaha!
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: That joke sounds like a hint. Could he be a Fool from the tavern?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Maybe, if we find the "fragile moon" he mentioned, we'll find the way into the tavern.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Sparkle's riddle says this... Whether looking up or down, they all see the same Phantasmoon when gazing at the sky.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We've gazed at the sky already, so next...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We go find where the Phantasmoon is.
Your curious gaze circles him. Is that thing by his side a... talking monkey?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: From this angle, the moon's reflection is right here. It does look strange in the water.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If what the card says is true, and the Fool's riddle is the key to entering the tavern, then this moon must be the door lock.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Come on, [Trailblazer], let's take a closer look at this strange "moon."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...So this is the "World's End" Tavern?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No, no, no, allow me to correct you. If you think this is all there is to the tavern, you're sorely mistaken.
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: Like a single grape on a great bunch, this is just the part where the tavern connects to this world...
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: Sorry, but this looks... like a regular lounge?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hahaha, the so-called "Planarcadia" isn't really an "arcadia" either, but who's complaining? Life goes on, doesn't it?
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: If you're looking for something that's "true to its name," take a ride on the Astral Express! Funny thing is, it's literally a train, you know? Can't find a single trace of astronautical engineering on it!
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: Uh... wait, you two are... Navigator of the Astral Express, and the raccoon on board, right? I've seen you in the news.
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: HAHAHA! Friends, a big shot is here! A real knee-slapper incoming!
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: Are they really from the Express? You're not some cosplay enthusiast, are you?
rows.speaker: Fools

rows.text: Express folks come to the tavern too? Do they even have a sense of humor?
rows.speaker: Fools

rows.text: Hey hey hey, can I get your autograph? Sign the sole of my foot! I'll never wash it again!
rows.speaker: Fools

rows.text: Everyone, curb your curiosity! These two are my guests. Even the most mischievous among you should know when to stop, and mind your manners!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You casually browse through the documents on your computer desktop, finding those unarchived medical records are a real parade of characters.
A patient claims to be Ena incarnate, and those who give them a thumbs up are blessed pathstriders of the Order.
The next record is even more absurd. The patient claims that HE is Ena, and that the person who claims to be Ena is actually Yaoshi who has gone mad.
Next page, the patient searches everywhere for the "Space Bar," believing that their system lacks a jump function. Next page...
Well, well, if it isn't little Sparkle? We've all heard your joke...
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: You instinctively look away. Some things are better left unknown.
Take the Mask from a Masked Fool, and what's left's but a fool...
rows.speaker: Stumbling Fool

rows.text: Oh my, wouldn't a Masked Fool be better off without the fool? An empty mask sounds even better, no?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Put him on mute for two hours. If no one flushes him down the "Golden Confessional," he'll be back to hassle me again in two hours.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Alive... ish? Depends how you define "alive." Most Fools won't even admit they're alive, so he isn't exactly dead either.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Don't take an idiot's words too seriously, unless you want to join them?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Alright, now I can finally entertain my guests without interruptions. You two, this way. Let's talk about the impostor.
rows.speaker: Sparkle
