rows.text: The man's weary gaze sizes up the young person before him for a moment. He offers a slight nod in greeting.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: A Slumbernana Monkey?
Your monkey can talk?
What's that?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: He's not mine. His freedom belongs to himself.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Kid, I believe you're confusing me with some other primates you've met.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Sorry, my mistake.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hey! What's going on! Why am I pinned here!?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Alright, you two, first round's on me. What'll it be?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Ha! This is a tavern. Even if you don't drink a drop, the Fools' jokes and pranks will turn your world upside down until you can't tell sky from ground!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Gray Hair, let's go. I don't want to waste any more time with this quack.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: We're not here to drink. Time's ticking. Did you find anything on Sparxie?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Bravo!
rows.speaker: Fool

rows.text: That's hilarious!
rows.speaker: Fool

rows.text: So, is it time for the combat sequence now?
rows.speaker: Sparkle Doll

rows.text: Phew! Miss Sparkle lives to fight another day!
rows.speaker: Sparkle Doll

rows.text: Don't pull a long face. You'll sour the vintage in the cask. While you were gone, diligent little Sparkle was gathering intel non-stop, and didn't waste a single minute.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Don't worry. I had old Gio open a shortcut.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I called Giovanni. You might not remember him... he's the poor sap who drew the short straw to manage the storage area recently. Old Gio told me that a week ago, "I" came here and took a few things...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Among them was a vial of memetic virus.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: A memetic virus... No wonder she could take over Graphia Academy and distort March and Welt's cognition, making them believe they're a student and teacher.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Close enough. The so-called "SparxiCon" is a front for spreading a memetic virus.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: This is Synwish Syndicate's turf.
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Can't believe people still have the guts to come here!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: People always come here looking for a "tavern"...
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: But no one's ever found it.
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Dovebrook's waters are my tears~
rows.speaker: Caustide

rows.text: I'm not drunk, hehe, I'm not drunk!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: No swimming in Dovebrook!
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: But if you insist on taking a dip, I can't stop you.
rows.speaker: Synwish Syndicate Member

rows.text: Knowing that isn't enough. What type of memetic virus is she spreading? What are the symptoms? We need more on her plans and actions before we can counter it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Thought of that already. So I visited a few friends and learned where the imposter's been haunting. To dig up details, we'll have to get hands-on.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Lead the way then.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's move. Stay close.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Well, that's a relief. Heh, not like I could tell if you were or stop you, right?
rows.speaker: Melancholic Door

rows.text: No, you're not Aha. Heh. You've got that smooth-talker air, but you're not.
rows.speaker: Melancholic Door

rows.text: The moon's reflection... so fragile, it shatters at a touch...
rows.speaker: Drunkard

rows.text: The staggering Fool lies quietly on the ground. Compared to before, he's become small and thin, a size perfect for carrying around.
Sparkle finds herself bound to the bed by an invisible force. This irresistible power you've experienced yourself on mornings when you just can't get up. No one can defeat it!
Sparkle was pinned to the bed! Who knows what trick Zhongshan pulled: invisible ropes from myths? An unseen giant hand? Telekinesis?
Isn't this the tavern of the Elation? Don't you welcome The Laughter gracing you with THEIR presence?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Uh? And then...?
rows.speaker: Melancholic Door

rows.text: Huh? What?
rows.speaker: Melancholic Door

rows.text: Wh—What are you going to do?
rows.speaker: Melancholic Door

rows.text: I'm gonna "break" you open.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Didn't expect you to have the pull to get me into the tavern. As expected of a detective's assistant.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Back when I still had a sense of humor, a Fool gave me an invitation. You can thank him for that.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: You're really going to see the Stellaron Hunter case through? They can only pay you in dirty money, you know.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: What else can I do? The boys need the money. Credits aren't black or white. They're ones and zeros.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: All right. I reached out to Caustide. He said that one of the three people who stole the mask looked familiar. He might've seen them in the news.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Based on his description, I spent ages sketching the suspect's portrait, and I suspect it might be Dan Heng, the Nameless from the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Ah, Caustide... We owe him another favor. No paying this one back, huh? Speaking of which, Dan Heng... That's a Xianzhou name, isn't it? Where have I heard that name before...? It sounds so familiar.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: It's just a door, what a lame joke collector. Maybe there's just some uninspired stand-up comedian hiding behind it, stealing inspiration from everyone who walks through?
That huge light orb up there! For a tavern, it's as essential as the Phantasmoon in the sky. If we get the chance, I can take you inside for a real eye-opener.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: So, which one of these three is Dan Heng? The one with gray hair? The redhead? Or that black-haired girl who looks like she's ready to stir up trouble at any moment?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: No, don't tell me yet. Let me guess.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I know a bit of the Xianzhou language. The word "dan" can mean "red." So Dan Heng... is the lady with red hair, right?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Your deduction skills never fail to impress. Fine, I'll just give you the answer. None of these three is Dan Heng. Do you even watch the news?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: TV, newspapers, the internet... it's all fake news. What do you expect me to look at?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Let's get down to business. I couldn't find any trace of Dan Heng's actions. It's like someone wiped them clean.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Nice work, Mister N. They're heading deeper into the tavern. Follow me.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I see, [Trailblazer]... the tavern not inviting you sooner was their loss.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You knew? And what made you link me to this place? That's kinda harsh, {M#bro.}{F#sis.}
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Come on in.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Is the drink in these barrels really brewed from jokes?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yep. You know your stuff, ma'am!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Just heard some rumors, that's all.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Doesn't the drinksmith care about this nonsense?
Watch out, {M#bro!}{F#sis!} Must be some weird thing a Fool dumped into the sewers, huh?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Can't Aha take care of this place?
You know how the Masked Fools are... Spiking drinks with hot sauce and tossing firecrackers down the toilet.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Being a drinksmith is a tough gig. No one volunteers. Since {RUBY_B#previous drinksmith}Bragi{RUBY_E#} vanished, the Fools have been drawing lots to take turns as temporary drinksmiths.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: {M#Bro,}{F#Girl,} what part of this is elating?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: ...Aha? Take care? Weren't THEY banned from the tavern?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: And given The Laughter's personality, if THEY "took care" of it, THEY'd just egg someone on to blow the place sky-high.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: This Fool you're talking about... It wouldn't happen to be Sparxie, would it?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If it were, I'd already be tied to that light orb as the scapegoat.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Anyway, the next stop is the Golden Confessional. The eyewitness says Sparxie was there.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The Golden Confessional... What kind of place is that?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A place where you can let go of all your worries. Well, words won't do it justice. Let's go see it for yourself.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: So many... sinks?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Why bring us here?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Witnesses say a week ago "I" came to the bar, knocked back a few shots of "Bomb's First Drop," then headed here.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The Golden Confessional is an emergency shelter for Fools who've had one drink too many. Here, we shed our excess baggage before marching light-footed into the next second.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Wait... isn't this just a bathroom?
A golden... throne?
Phew, it doesn't smell as bad as I imagined...
The Golden Confessional is THE Golden Confessional, not some random bathroom!
Well well, looks like ol' Sampo's become the king without a crown!
Of course! This is just a place where everyone comes to let off some steam.
Well, well, if it isn't my old friend! Sparkle said you'd be coming to the tavern. Old Sampo's heart is bursting with joy!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: On a trip, I met a girl who shared my tastes. She had quite the knack to be a Fool.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Missed me, old friend?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Hello, Miss Himeko. Long time no see.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Mr. Sampo, hello. What business brings you here this time?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No business, just here to repay an old favor.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: [Trailblazer], wake up!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Shush, Sampo. I brought you here to repay a favor, not to gossip about me.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Oh, I've suffered the embarrassment of losing my mask myself. Thanks to Miss Sparkle's mercy, I didn't end up stranded. So here I am today, ready to help you out, no questions asked!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Alright then, let's get to work!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Get to work? What are we doing?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Naturally... We'll fish around in these "thrones" where humans dump their worries and find the worries that Miss Sparxie left behind.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: You want us to... unclog your toilet?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Here? Dig up worries?
Don't even joke about that!
Angular and blocky, it hurts to hold, with a slight stinging sensation, like stepping on a small toy part hidden in the carpet.
I'm not joking.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Don't be too shocked, you two. Let me share a little secret about how we Masked Fools stay mentally healthy...
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Drink a mood-lifter like "Bomb's First Drop," and all the harmful memoria in your body — you know, the pain, the worries — gets purged in one go.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: That's how Fools pull pranks and have a blast without a shred of guilt.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: So all that memoria has settled under this bathroom. And you want to sift through it to find Sparxie's worries... and catch her thoughts before she acts?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If luck's on our side, maybe we'll even dig up the secret to beating her. What's wrong, ma'am? You don't look so hot.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I've got no objection to the task, but... doing this bare-handed? I refuse.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Don't worry, when has ol' Sampo ever come unprepared? Trust me, I won't let you get off that easy!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Emotional Impact Drill!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Sorry, wrong gadget. This one.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Hey, have you heard of a dowsing rod? Well ...Forget it, I'll spare you the theory.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: I tuned the drill bit to resonate with Sparkle's temperament. It'll drill out memoria fountains with similar emotions.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: But fair warning: Use it carefully! It's been a week since Sparxie was here. Keep your guard up in case something else comes bursting out.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: With so many toilets, where do we start?
Well, If you ask me... leave it to luck.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: We don't have time for luck. My radar says that pompous imposter would pick the highest spot to vent...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Exactly, the "Golden Throne." Give it a try!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Sampo, does this thing even work?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Of course it works! Don't you trust your old pal Sampo?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Huh? That doesn't seem like something she'd be worried about.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: After going through all this trouble to sneak in... Thought I'd go down in a blaze of glory if I got caught...
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: ...What the heck is going on with this place!? Have the Masked Fools really fallen this far?
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: You are...?
Me? I'm a Mourning Actor! Isn't it obvious?
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: Not in the least.
What exactly makes you "mourning"?
Can't you tell? I'm very sad right now!
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: No thanks. I'd like to stay sober.
I'm underage. A glass of water please.
Let me tell you about my tragic mission: After the tavern issued a ban on Mourning Actors, I painstakingly snuck in here to reveal to them the truth that "destiny is eternally sorrowful."
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: Sparxie... She did come here disguised as me.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You pulled it off!?
I failed! I smashed every obstacle during the infiltration, only for the outcome to smash me!
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: Yesterday, I went on stage at the bar and revealed my true identity to everyone and told them a tragic tale, bracing myself for their harshest punishment and farthest exile.
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: She wants to turn everyone into monkeys?
But they... these Fools kept whistling from below, and some bought me several rounds. Someone even came up on stage to hug me, praising me as "the unprecedented Masked Fool".
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: This is... utterly humiliating!
rows.speaker: Melancholic Worries

rows.text: Sampo, how did you get up there just now?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Oh right, silly me. Through that pipe on the side.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Come out, Sparxie's worries!
See? What did I tell you? The impostor's worries have appeared!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: What a rare sight! Sparxicle used to always connect with everyone online. But now, for the first time, she's meeting her fans through the sewer network!
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: Sorry, but we're your haters!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Come clean now! What are you planning to do with that memetic virus you stole? Use SparxiCon as a front to turn everyone into mindless zombies, or dancing monkeys?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: How could I ever harm my dearest, most beloved fans?
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: They feel insecure about being ordinary, cry when ignored by those they like, and strive to stand out because they desperately want others' approval...
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: No. I'll give each of them a choice... the choice to become "me."
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: For reals? She plans to use a memetic virus to turn everyone into herself?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Ah, the answer was right there in the riddle all along! ...y'know, I gotta say, that's very Sparkle.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: As expected of my impostor. You're absolutely bonkers!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Sis, is now the time to be tooting your own horn? Just thinking about being turned into a copy of you... I can't even force a smile!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: So I decided to try a different approach. Keep tabs on the other members of the Express Crew. Maybe following their trail will lead to clues about the mask.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Oh? And who gets to define "elation"? The Laughter? The Fools? The IPC? Or... every "me" seeking joy on the arcadian internet?
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: Where's this...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Ta-da! Welcome to the dazzling lights of the "Blisstar"!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The heart of the tavern, Planarcadia's dazzling dance floor. There are some tasteless Masked Fools who consider this place the secret to keeping the laughter going...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: If life's cruel, don't beg for fairness. Dance! Shake away that sadness until it's all well-mixed with the joy in your body.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Blisstar?
Speaking of which, two months ago some idiot, after downing hundreds of drinks, had the bright idea to knock it down with a Super Overlord Spinning Top.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: So we had to reinforce the Blisstar with a steel frame around it and seal it inside the World in Canvas.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Contrary to popular belief, the masters of the Phantasmoon Games were never us, the Supplicants, but the spectators watching us.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: Sadly, the Interastral Peace Network showed people other worlds in the cosmos. Once horizons widen, expectations climb... nothing they hear or see feels fresh, interesting, or thrilling enough.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: And everyone fears that they're outdated, uninteresting, or unexciting in others' eyes.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: Bingo, you got it! I'm a part of her...
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries (?)

rows.text: Wherever there's a screen, wherever my audience is... my eyes and ears will be there too.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Madness

rows.text: I want to see how far you and this outdated model can go. The harder you struggle, the more spectacular it'll be when I livestream the Astral Express crew's "derailment" at SparxiCon!
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Madness

rows.text: I'm looking forward to your resistance, Nameless.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Madness

rows.text: Heads up, everyone! She's getting serious!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Listen Sparkle, you only asked me to do your "dirty work," but you never said anything about being your thug! You owe me compensation for emotional damage.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Everyone's going to become "me" soon! Sampo, crawl out of your money pit for a moment, will you?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: To think Planarcadia's "Elation" would end up like this...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Back when I still lived in this place, the internet was just for sharing information. Live-streaming and virtual idols? We'd never even heard of them...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Coming back now feels like stepping into a foreign land... like returning home only to find home isn't where it used to be.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And a teensy bit of sorrow. How did Sparkle beat me to inviting my number-one {M#buddy}{F#bestie} to the tavern for a drink?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Sampo, it's you!
I knew I'd find you here!
Either way... this is definitely not elation.
It's just madness wrapped in a cheerful shell...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Miss Fool here sent me a message asking for h-e-l-p. Someone's been parading around the tavern, impersonating her.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Well, now this is some juicy news! Miss Sparkle's usually the one impersonating others, but look how the tables have turned. The trickster's getting a taste of her own medicine!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: She's convinced that we'll be powerless to stop her plan even if we know what it is, but I'm not ready to roll over just yet.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I know, I know. Even I don't want to turn into that phony's look-alike... though we're not that different.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Since the Fools stash dangerous things like memetic viruses in the tavern, I assume they must've also prepared some countermeasures?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Alright, alright, now that you folks have a lead and no shortage of fighting spirit, old Sampo's calling it a day.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: You aren't coming with us?
The Astral Express always has a way of handling crisis-es, doesn't it? With the big shots here, a sidekick like me doesn't need to steal the spotlight.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: If you run into real trouble, you can always ring old Sampo then. Hehe, I'll even give you folks a special discount... Sorta.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Well then, farewell, everyone!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: So, where are we heading next?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...Let's check out "Fatal Joke."
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Fatal Joke? What kind of place is that?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Maybe... some kind of "hospital."
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: ...Why is there a hospital hidden inside the tavern?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Every time someone goes bonkers and stirs up trouble in the tavern, like scattering nosewalker parasite ticks in every corner, or spiking the beer barrels with truth serum that makes people spew insults...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: For each time the whole place goes topsy-turvy, there's always some Fool who, in the spirit of the Elation, volunteers to treat them. Yep, they get sent right here, to "Fatal Joke."
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Strange, why isn't there even a fake doctor around today?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Even if some Fool claims to have a legit medical license, you wouldn't dare trust them, would you?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Attention patients: Please refrain from eating beef hotpot in the hallway. If you wish to dine, please invite the hospital director to join you. Thank you.
rows.speaker: Hospital PA System

rows.text: Would Dr. Hartman from Plastic Surgery please report to the director's office immediately? This hospital doesn't even have a plastic surgery department... Who on earth are you?
rows.speaker: Hospital PA System

rows.text: Dr. Zhongshan from Mental Health Care, please report to Exam Room 1. We're one player short for cards. Thank you.
rows.speaker: Hospital PA System

rows.text: ...Is this a theater or a hospital?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Alert! Patient detected ahead! Patient detected ahead! Please line up in an orderly fashion for registration and wait for the doctor to begin consultations.
rows.speaker: Hospital PA System

rows.text: {M#Bro,}{F#Girl,} pick a spot to drill and start mining that gold!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Violent splashing sounds came from the bucket, as if human worries were about to burst forth.
Suddenly, something emerged from the sewer!
Come forth, Sparxie's worries!
Violent splashing sounds came from the bucket, as if human worries were about to burst forth.
Suddenly, something emerged from the sewer!
You draw near the throne that is radiating an aura of supreme power. It's unquestionably made of solid gold.

Every atom that makes it up came from neutron star collisions and supernova bursts... Yet the Masked Fools forged these precious tears of the stars into vessels to hold human worries. Perhaps in their eyes, this was their way of playing a cosmic joke.
You notice a problem: Compared to the towering throne, you're way too small to reach and dip the Drill Bit into the water.
I'm your presiding physician.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Haha, [Trailblazer]! Talk about fate! Ever since our little escapade with the Unshackled on the Xianzhou, I've been wondering when someone as interesting as you would grace our tavern.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: The golden throne emanates a dazzling aura of authority. You're genuinely afraid you might slip and fall right into it.
You forcefully thrust the drill bit into the toilet!
Suddenly, the toilet starts gushing water violently, and something emerges from the drain!
Good news for you: you don't need to rush into treatment just yet. Though I can't say the same for Miss Sparkle over there.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Is this... Duomension City? How is that possible?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The tavern's spatial structure is bizarre to begin with. It's not that strange to see Duomension City here.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: No way... Are these... General Yao Guang's medical records?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Miss Sparkle, please wait in this room until the consultation is complete.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: You took an entire school of teachers and students hostage and turned them into your puppets to help you enter the Phantasmoon Games. You're going to argue that you did it all "for them"?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Of course I did! From the very first day I was created, I've been doing exactly what my creator asked of me: listening to every fan's questions, empathizing with their pain and troubles.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: Hey there! Are you also troubled by the same illness as me?
rows.speaker: Weak Mask

rows.text: Sparxie hears every wish, and she answers!
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: During these Phantasmoon Games, I'll grant their wishes through the Ceremony of the Master of Elation...
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: With a memetic virus?
Because deep down, every one of them longs to become Sparxie. To wear this dazzling mask, capture the internet's attention, and bask in praise.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: You must have heard that saying: "In the future, everyone gets their fifteen minutes of fame."
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: Now, that moment has come. SparxiCon will turn every spectator into me.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: What illness do you have?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I once suffered from a disease called "Fool."
rows.speaker: Weak Mask

rows.text: What kind of disease is "Fool"?

A Masked Fool named "Sparkle" grew out of me, slowly becoming one with me. She used me to bear all the pain caused by her performances, left me battered and bruised, while she slipped away from everything...
rows.speaker: Weak Mask

rows.text: This is sooo elating!
This isn't Elation.
But I was lucky enough to find this tumor called "Sparkle," and I... expelled this malignant growth from my body.
rows.speaker: Weak Mask

rows.text: You're just a tool I discarded!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Sparkle, do you still remember me?
rows.speaker: Sad Mask

rows.text: So the world's like a derailed train, racing toward thrills and madness... Nameless of the Astral Express, am I wrong?
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Worries

rows.text: Would a bundle of worries even recognize us?
More people got my name right today than in the past week! I'm so touched!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I am your original mask... the "Sparkle Role" mask.
rows.speaker: Sad Mask

rows.text: The Sparkle role?
The archetype of a bright maiden doomed for a short life: the avenger who perishes with her nemesis, the lover who dies for love, the young artist driven to madness...
rows.speaker: Sad Mask

rows.text: The worst thing an actor should do is be tied down to one type of role.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Do yourself a favor and stay down!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Hehe, Sparkle, you're back!
rows.speaker: Smiling Mask

rows.text: You seem happy.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Is it really happy?
Y—Yeah. I'm keeping my spirits high, just like she asked!
rows.speaker: Smiling Mask

rows.text: Sparkle, Sparkle, you're the one who told me that a smiling mask will never have bad luck, aren't you?
rows.speaker: Smiling Mask

rows.text: This world doesn't want to see too much sadness, cruelty, rage, or pain... You told me that I just need to smile, no matter what.
rows.speaker: Smiling Mask

rows.text: I did everything you asked... but why did you abandon me? Right now... Right now, I just want to scream! To cry! To shout!
rows.speaker: Smiling Mask

rows.text: Haha, ma'am, you give us Fools too much credit. This is the tavern, not the well-ordered Herta Space Station.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: But I do know a place! With some luck, we might find a memetic virus clean-up expert.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Just how many masks have you thrown away?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Don't worry about it! Everyone sheds just as many versions of themselves in a lifetime...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Miss Sparkle, I have your results. Your main components are madness, humor, and a theatrical personality. Unfortunately, the proportions are badly imbalanced. You're beyond saving.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: But the silver lining is, your mask has fallen off! She's free at last!
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: And that's where everyone's misfortune began. None of the masks I've cast off ever had such strong opinions or such a temper.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Well, because those who can become Fools are all a bit sick in the head. Not your regular headaches and fevers, but... matters of the heart.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: She no longer needs to be corroded by your cancer of rationality. Now, she can do anything that you wanted to do but didn't dare to do.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Ha! As if there's anything Miss Sparkle wouldn't dare to do!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: For example... you don't dare wear any one mask for too long.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: ...Fake?

Like a butterfly shedding old skin, you keep discarding every mask, just so you won't be defined or bound by them. You're afraid to stop, to be stuck in some stereotype. You're afraid that one day you won't be "elating" enough...
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: As a dazzling mask, everyone confides in her, everyone wants to be her, everyone feeds her their clever ideas. You thought this would inject new life into your "elation"...
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: But sadly, once the mask is on, you become its accessory. People care only about the image the mask paints. No one cares about the you beneath.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: And that is why she came to life!
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Human recognition and desire will flow through the internet, providing nourishment for her to bloom: She'll become a bewitching flower, conforming to everyone's wishes, letting them wear her, become her, and blossom across all of Planarcadia! What a beautiful sight...
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Patient #01: Akivili! Is there a {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Akivili?
rows.speaker: "Nurse"

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Akivili, diagnosed with Stellaron symptoms per the records, are you present? Please proceed to Exam Room 1.
rows.speaker: "Nurse"

rows.text: ...They called you by name, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} "Akivili." You might as well go take a look.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Doctor, do you have a way to stop her?
"Stop"? You mean... "treat," yes?
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Cremate Sparkle. That's the best treatment I can prescribe.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Pfft. And here I thought you had something clever.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: After all, there's only one radical cure for all suffering: make oneself disappear, right?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Miss Sparkle, don't think I'm joking around with you. I only misbehave outside the tavern.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: But here I am a doctor, without quotation marks. My treatment is real and effective. Generally, when a Fool vanishes, their mask loses its power and becomes a dead thing. You're two sides of the same coin, after all.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: But as for "Sparxie"... I can't say for sure. During SparxiCon, she'll be worn by millions of ordinary people in Planarcadia, feeding her with sustenance and strength. Your window of opportunity is therefore fleeting...
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: There's a door in the tavern that absolutely, positively, leads to a still-burning star in Sedounirama. The "nurse" will send you there, and that'll be the end of it.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: And if I say no?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You used me to win fame, applause, and countless eager gazes... so why would you cruelly cast me aside?
rows.speaker: Sad Mask

rows.text: Please, wear me once more...
rows.speaker: Sad Mask

rows.text: Then I'll have to... be impolite.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Gray Hair? Ma'am Navigator? A little help?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You need me! I can help you defeat Sparxie!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The mask of the Masked Fool represents what you wish to become. You use it to focus your power, but the mask will gradually bind you as well.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's why you've been avoiding Sparxie all this time. She didn't just steal a vial of memetic virus... She stole your strength.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No wonder the Fool at the bar joked: when a Masked Fool loses their mask, what remains is just a fool.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It might be a Mourning Actor mask you took a liking to and stole from them. It might be a head accessory you personally sketched in a moment of inspiration. Or it might be something that one day fell from the sky and latched onto your face...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: To become a Fool, one must experience at least one such instance of destiny: the moment of masking one's face.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I just want to... DEVOUR YOU WHOLE!!!
rows.speaker: No-Longer-Smiling Mask

rows.text: Through the mask's eyeholes, we gain a different perspective, finally seeing how the universe is simply churning with endless jokes and the absurd nature of our existence as living beings.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The mask is what we want to be. And now, this impostor is more "me" than I am.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Do it! Press the button, call the nurse, and cremate Miss Sparkle!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: At least then the impostor will lose her power for a little while. You should be able to take her down easily, right?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Uh... you're not actually going to press it, right?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: She's not just your virtual persona...
Give us a moment... to hesitate, to think.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Waiting is torture, you know. You're not doing this on purpose to punish me, are you? Hey, Gray Hair! Say something!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Hahaha, I knew it! Gray Hair, you're still the same warm-hearted Gray Hair I know!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: ...That's why you drew Miss "Sparxie," and became her online.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: Unbelievable! Gray Hair, is your heart colder than Belobog's Ice Out of Space!?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Hehe, I took the battery out of the button earlier while no one watched. It was a test, and you failed!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Hey hey hey! Gray Hair, have you forgotten our friendship? You'll make the button smoke at this rate!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Too bad. I took the battery out of the button earlier while no one watched. It was a test, and you failed!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Since the Fool made her choice, she must have a plan to reclaim the Mask, right?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If you dare say "no," I'll press THIS button and let the orbital cannon "cremate" you for real. Your sticky little fingers aren't fast enough to steal this battery, are they?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: There's a way! There's always a way!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Miss Sparkle will definitely take responsibility and work together with everyone to stop SparxiCon!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: What's with this applause?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Have we... been watched the whole time?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: So the audience watched our every move in that "treatment"? ...Is this a hospital or a theater?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Go on, lie down on that bed and say goodbye to your friends. Press that button, and the "nurse" will come wheel you away.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: That's life for you. While there's life, there's judgment. In every unseen corner, countless judging eyes are watching, diagnosing, and writing their own "prescriptions."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I must admit, Fatal Joke is a fascinating place. Real shame I didn't come check it out earlier.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Ignore the spectators. They're just here for laughs. They won't help, and couldn't if they tried.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Miss Sparkle, [Trailblazer], the choice is yours. As for me... By The Laughter above, I've got to catch the next ship out of this dump.
rows.speaker: Zhongshan

rows.text: You said you had a way to stop Sparxie. Let's hear it. What's the plan?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I've got a few... "Anti-Sparkle Weapons" in my collection.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: What's that?
Yes, every Fool has at least one such mask. Not mere decoration, but a part of our destiny, crafted by our own hands...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Why would you go against yourself?
The name says it all. These are items Miss Sparkle collected in my past adventures, and weapons that my fierce rivals once used against me.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I've always had this premonition that one day Miss Sparkle would become an unstoppable terror in this universe. Someone has to find a way to stop me before that day comes!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: In our battle of wits, she nearly turned me into Sparkle paste using the local "Tumbleweed" specialty. She also had a massive mech with beam cannons up the wazoo, ready to blast away any time.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I quietly replicated those powerful goodies from my travels. With these Anti-Sparkle Weapons, that impostor won't know what hit her!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I gotta say, I'm quite the visionary!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You two, let's head to the storage area next. I've already contacted Giovanni. He's doing an inventory check of the lost items there.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Intel from the school?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The furbo journalist couldn't find March or Mr. Yang, but they did spot Sparxie taking down the wave painting in the school courtyard.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Don't press the button)
Psst, let me tell you something. While no one was looking, I already popped the battery out of the button. This was a test, and you passed!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: (Press the button)
Oh? That's noteworthy. Looks like Sparxie's busy making preparations too. But why do all this?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: (Frantically mashing buttons!)
Never mind her for now. Let's check out the Fools' storage area.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hey, Gio. What are you doing up there?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Working my tail off for you, tallying the losses! Wait, who'd you bring with you?
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Oh, it's [Trailblazer]! I knew you'd step into the tavern and become one of us someday. Those with the makings of Masked Fools are naturally drawn to one another.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: [Trailblazer], you sure know quite a few Fools.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And the lovely lady behind you... you must be Miss Himeko, Navigator of the Express. A pleasure to meet you.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Mr. Giovanni, just call me Himeko.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Normally only Fools may enter, but since Sparkle brought you, and [Trailblazer] is practically an old friend, I can make an exception as the caretaker. Let me show you around...
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Want the Fools' treasure, souvenirs, and prank gear? Come to the Grand Treasury storage! They've stashed everything here.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You stole my line again.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Are you trying to advertise to thieves or what?
That line... sounds familiar?
Pfft. With our theft rate, that tagline's probably to blame.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Picked it up on a trip to another world. You've heard this phrase too, haven't you?
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: I'll admit, it's catchy. That's why I used it as a slogan. Storage area visits went up by 26% after that.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Business first. Did you see my pickup message I sent? Where's my stored Anti-Sparkle Weapons?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Your storage list is a total mess. You never leave any notes! If I hadn't been called to audit, who'd know how many surprises you got stashed away? As for the "Anti-Sparkle Weapons"... I'd love to know what on earth that's supposed to be?
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Bah, why don't you go in and look for yourself!
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: As requested, I've linked the vault entrance to your collection room.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: The undercover journalist didn't find the hostages.
Gio, did the impostor leave this behind?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: How should I know? I've been doing inventory all this time. I only just now noticed something fishy about this thing.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Huh. What's this?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Whoa, that's one massive Stellar Jade!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let's go in and take a look.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: This rock... is dangerous.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Dangerous? I'll smash it with one swing!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You got it. Smash it and bring it all back.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Enjoy the surprise gift? Haha, Stellar Jade is the perfect bait for catching the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Voice

rows.text: Gio, cut the spiel. Sampo says you recite that intro so often he's grown calluses on his ears...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: How generous of you. First time I've seen a thief steal something and leave something even more valuable in the vault.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Isn't this exactly the type of phantom-thief flair we Masked Fools adore? Remove a carefully curated piece, and leave a gift in place to soothe the owner.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Voice

rows.text: Heh, a jumbo-sized Stellar Jade is surely worth a jar of Memetic Virus and a few "Anti-Sparkle Weapons," wouldn't you say?
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Voice

rows.text: ...And you stole my other prized pieces too!?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: That worthless junk? Consider it a complimentary vault cleaning.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Voice

rows.text: Before SparxiCon begins, I'd like a little warm-up entertainment. Old model, and the Nameless, you should be able to break out of this room, right? Don't disappoint me now.
rows.speaker: Sparxie's Voice

rows.text: Gio, the security here is an absolute mess!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You're in no position to talk. Even the drinksmith here is a temp. Count yourself lucky I'm kind enough to help tally your storage.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Stellar Jade... There are many theories about where these gems came from. Some say they're light that cooled and crystallized after the primordial universe took shape. Others claim they're the crystallized essence of ancient leviathans, formed over billions of years.
Without a doubt, its mesmerizing beauty could be traded for everything in this universe — material pleasures, Light Cones of the Garden, ancient Relics, and the devotion of others...
There's such a huge one right in front of you, big enough to drive everyone crazy... That's right, you want it! You really want it! You're about to go into a frenzy—
My precioussss...
...Huh?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: She didn't just steal my power and my collection... she completely destroyed Miss Sparkle's reputation! This is... the worst day ever!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Correction: Miss Sparkle's "worst day so far."
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Want to make fun of me? Go ahead.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: As expected of Himeko. You have a backup plan?
You can fight fire with fire, but a memetic virus can be scoured away with "water."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What do you mean?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Our informant at the school reports Sparxie is removing the central painting there.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The imagenated painting "Worldbreaker Waves" is said to be a work left behind by Graphia herself. Legend says the wave comes from the Dovebrook river-water she used to wash off her painting mistakes. The artists say it is blessed. That's why they kept it in the school.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I couldn't understand why Sparxie went to such lengths to tear it down. Now I do. "Painting mistakes" are redundant information that stain a painting. A memetic virus is redundant information that stains the mind.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If someone knew how to harness this Dovebrook wave to wash over the school, they could cleanse the infection she spread. That's why Sparxie wanted to hide the painting.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So the solution lies within the school?
Maybe we can ask Dan Heng to use cloudhymn?
Don't get me wrong. I also don't think "gear tumbleweeds" and "giant mechs" would work on someone spreading memetic viruses.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I thought of a way just now that might suppress the memetic contagion at Graphia Academy...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Exactly.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The waves on the painting aren't physical water. Only those versed in the art of imagenesis can control them.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As a Graphia Academy alumna, I know a bit of traditional painting. Right now, our most directly effective plan is to break into the school, regain control of the painting, and use it to suppress Sparxie's movements.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's go! I'll make this impostor pay a hundred-fold!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Looks like our paths must part in haste. I wish you all fair winds on your journey ahead.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Oh! If any of you feel uncertain about what's next, here's a small suggestion: Take a detour inside the "Blisstar" light orb.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: We don't have time to waste.
And what is that place?
A quick prayer to the gods before battle hardly counts as wasting time, does it?
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: For us Masked Fools, that light orb holds the same significance as the Phantasmoon hanging above.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: Deep within the orb, everyone can find the divine revelations of the Elation.
rows.speaker: Giovanni

rows.text: This doesn't look like where we came in...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Darn it...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: They found something else at the school?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The undercover journalist got caught.
We need to pick up the pace.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Giovanni said we could find the divine revelations of the Elation inside the light orb? Don't tell me this orb is another tavern room?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: With trembling unease, you reach into the gaping fissure. Just pretend it's like the mouth of that Amphorean Verax Leo, you keep telling yourself.
Bingo! Your intuition's spot-on. It isn't just a light-polluting orb. Think of it as a shrine for Fools.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Your hand seems to plunge into a soft, swirling fluid, and a bizarre monkey screech echoes in your ears, reminding you of an ominous story about wish-making. Then you sense that you've touched something.
The youngsters only revoked The Laughter's right to enter the tavern. They don't reject things associated with THEM.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Pfft, "worship" sounds a bit too serious, no?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: You know for sure you've seen this thing before, right there in Penacony.

The extraordinary experience of fighting alongside "The Dazzling Ninja" AKA Rappa against the "Osaru Evil Ninja" flashed through your mind. The answer, like a banana hanging in the sky, compelled you to reveal its origin—
That banana... I've seen it before...
To fight virus with virus...
Inside this light orb is a miracle tied to Aha. It responds to any Fool who approaches.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Let me show you something mind-blowing. Here we go. Open sesame...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I said! O-PEN! SE-SA-ME! Open sesame... Sesame? Open?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: ...No way! So in THEIR eyes I don't even count as a Masked Fool anymore? What a "wonderful surprise"! The impostor stole my identity too!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The good news is, at least one of us is still a Masked Fool.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hey, that's way too harsh!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: I hate to admit it... but Gray Hair, it's opened for you. The light orb has acknowledged you.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Just stick your hand in there.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Well, I gotta do something, right? *shriek* Like this?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Whatever floats your boat. Now listen up, you three. Put that banana down and walk away, and I'll let bygones be bygones.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: But if you try anything funny...
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: If you wanna get to them, you'll have to get through these little toys first!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Ready to try your luck? Reach into the fissure, and you'll find a gift from The Laughter.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Reach your hand in there...
Hold on, let me take a deep breath.
Akivili have mercy... in Akivili's name... please don't hurt me... My hand doesn't taste good...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Is this...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Huh. What's this?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yo {M#bro,}{F#sis,} just how many troublemakers did you people manage to tick off when you landed?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: The Laughter above, THEY really answered! But what's THEIR deal giving you another memetic virus?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Ah, now I get it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Audiences infected with the Sparxie Virus naturally won't be able to resist Sparxie... We'd end up like that soon after breaking into the school. But if we're already infected with another memetic virus... Well, that changes things.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And this banana serves exactly that purpose... to buy us some time to resist.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Elation really has a twisted sense of humor, huh? All right, let's move!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Who are you two? Haven't you heard the rule? Only one Fool's allowed in here at a time.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Who am I? Just a passing detective, and his assistant.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Have I been asleep too long? Or has humanity sunk so low they don't even care if they turn into monkeys?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Meanwhile, the ignorant criminals believed they had discovered a "treasure" that could change their destiny, completely unaware that what they held in their hands could shatter the sanity of the entire world.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Hey, Mister N, cut the narration when it's time to fight.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Tch, are these folks really the Nameless? In all my years, I've never seen the Nameless dealing with memetic viruses.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: The real deal. Just some Nameless passing through.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Mister N, I've got to go after them. You won't be able to keep up with me. Just head home and wait for the news.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I swear I won't let the tragedy that happened to you repeat itself in this world.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Over here! This way! Run faster! You don't wanna get caught by that guy back there, do you?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: So who was that just now?
Didn't you leave already?
When push comes to shove, Sampo's the one we can count on...
I swear, Miss Sparkle definitely hasn't gotten involved with someone like that.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: My eyelid's been twitching all day. Knew something was bound to go wrong. You know old Sampo's got a soft spot for his regulars, so I couldn't help but come check on you folks. And what do you know? I was right.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Good ol' Sampo came through with top-notch service, saving your lives in the nick of time.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Most Masked Fools treat The Laughter like an invisible, mischievous drinking buddy. Fine for a mental toast, but if THEY really come looking for you, it's usually bad news.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Thank you, Mr. Sampo.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Now that we're all set, it's time to head to Graphia Academy for the rescue mission. Mr. Sampo, do you know which door in the tavern can get us back to the city the quickest?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Haha, you don't even need to ask! When it comes to knowing all the "secret passages" and "shortcuts" in this tavern, you won't find anyone who can match old Sampo...
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Then lead the way!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Two similar figures clashed together, battling fiercely amidst swirling smoke and chaos, making it impossible to tell one from the other. From within the fray, faint voices could be heard...
A mere mask dares to threaten its master with such arrogance!?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Your thoughts tell me that you still have doubts about me.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Did you ask to meet here so I could clear up some of your doubts?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: ...Greetings, Lady Yao Guang.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Being able to hear others' thoughts anytime... this "tuning" ability sure comes in handy.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Someone carelessly tossed a comic magazine on the table.
"July 20th, 1984, Issue #29, introducing the brand new series Super Leaf Walkers!"... Man, that's such an old-school comic.
There's a notebook in the desk, with a sticky note attached to a page of the calendar.
"50th Anniversary Preparations... Purchase streamers, lanterns... Student exhibition planning... 84/07/16"
Compared to the Seer Strategist's ability to come and go as she pleases, this is nothing but a parlor trick.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The wispae called "Emoti" lets out a sharp, shrill snicker.
I've heard that Xianzhou folks are big on etiquette. Yet here I am, and you're still playing hide-and-seek. General, isn't that a bit discourteous?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Sorry... I have this old problem of suddenly disappearing. It's really something beyond my control.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: "Emoti" bursts into soft, whiny sobs.
As for the reason, I'm afraid I can't disclose it. Please forgive my rudeness.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Or, if you're truly that curious, why not use your "tuning" and find out?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You know I won't do that.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Besides, I couldn't even if I wanted to right now.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Couldn't?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: At this moment, the crowd's thoughts are crashing over me like a tidal wave.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I can't block out all this mental noise. Just keeping my own thoughts from getting tangled up in everyone else's is hard enough.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I see. So that's why, when you were speaking with Miss Himeko earlier, I accidentally intruded on your "private conversation."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Did you hear? The {M#guy}{F#girl} who beat Sparxie is the original inspiration for the protagonist in Fluffy Across the Blue. You know... that raccoon!
rows.speaker: Whispering Student

rows.text: {M#He's crazy cool!}{F#She's such a badass!}
rows.speaker: Whispering Student

rows.text: My "tuning" is spiraling out of control. This mask... is distorting my abilities.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm really curious about that "classroom frozen in time from fifteen years ago."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: [Trailblazer], just let me know when you're ready to head out.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's go now.
Give me a moment.
...I see it differently. The loss of control is temporary. That mask is amplifying your power.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: How is this possible? This "tuning" power is bestowed by the Harmony. How could the Elation meddle with THEIR authority?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Evil, take flight, Sparxie blazes bright!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Fan

rows.text: You people... get a grip!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Sparxicle! Sparxicle! Sparxicle!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Fan

rows.text: Perhaps the Elation simply poured more "fuel" into this divine authority?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: In my humble opinion, this mask binds the Supplicant to all beings of Planarcadia, drawing strength from those who share the same Path here for your use.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: That's why you're hearing others' thoughts surge toward you like a tide... Your "tuning" is steadily expanding, and you've become the center of this melody.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You sure gave me quite the "gift," general.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But why would such a precious gift be placed on my face...? I need an honest answer.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You want to know the reason? Didn't I explain it already?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Your reasons about me make sense, but what I really want is your answer... about yourself.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: General of the Yuque who sees into the future... why not wear the mask yourself and personally step into the fray with its power?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Mr. Sunday, why not use your enhanced "tuning" to feel the weight of that answer for yourself?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Well then... pardon my intrusion, Lady Yao Guang.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ah... so this bird on my shoulder is the manifestation of the "tuning's" resonance?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Are we really using that? If we don't take down that impostor before the virus hits, we'll all be monkeys in the jungle.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Exactly. And these symbols I see floating above people's heads...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Would be the "Weal and Woe Signs" you mentioned, general?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That's right. To become an Arbiter-General, one must undergo three ceremonies: the "Rainbow Ordainment," the "Reignbow's Gaze," and the "Bestowal of Spiritus." Only then can one truly take up the mantle and live up to the title.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: When I was appointed as the Yuque's general, I was bestowed with the Reignbow Spiritus called "Kālacakra Skyplume," which represents the vision of the Hunt among the seven aspects of the Reignbow: a symbol of foresight, verdict, and self-discipline.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Thanks to that, I gained the "Eye of Īśvara," which allows me to read the flow of destiny.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Since the day I arrived on this world, every person I've seen bore a crimson "Woe Sign" above their head without exception. Within days at most, a catastrophic disaster will befall this place.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: So, that red glow rising from the edge of the city is...?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The gap in the door seems filled with an impenetrable darkness, and you can't see a thing.
You hear what sounds like light raindrops gently falling on the window.
The classroom door won't budge an inch, no matter how much force you apply to it.
The blazing light formed by the convergence of all those "Woe Signs" in Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Mr. Sunday, have you heard the diviners' iron law? "Never divine the same matter twice"?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: In Penacony, diviners also warn clients beforehand: You can't ask for another spread just because you dislike the result. There's a reason for that, isn't there?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Divining the future is, in essence, a form of observation and calculation. It's an interference with the future. Each reading drives the murky future toward a definite outcome, a collapsed quantum state, even if that outcome isn't to one's liking.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: To be honest, when I set out for Planarcadia, I had fully intended to personally participate in the Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: ...You're saying that, simply by your observation, our future would become fixed?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Its gaze shifts awkwardly away, but a smug grin sneaks onto its lips, as if thinking: "You've got no knees? Pfft, good luck reaching for the moon."
Indeed, just like how {RUBY_B#Nous}the Wisdomwalker{RUBY_E#} expounded the way of destiny, anchoring the fated moments.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: If I wore the mask, I would become the Nous of Planarcadia, and I would "personally anchor" a destiny that drives us all into a bottomless darkness. We will become locked in a dead end with not a shred of hope for salvation.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Close one. I passed the trial. There's still a sliver of hope in this round.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: ...Now that makes me even more curious.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Pardon my bluntness, but the fate of billions in Planarcadia never had much to do with you, General. Your encounter with the Express and the IPC was merely a chance meeting.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You are a messenger of the Xianzhou. Since you foresaw the omen — that "an Arbiter General will fall here" — you could have boarded your ship and left at any time...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Why choose to stay and help us? To help this world break free of this deathtrap?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Because... I am guided by great compassion. Every life is precious beyond measure...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Such diplomatic pleasantries won't fool the former master of Penacony like yourself, would they?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Then, how about this reason? The Astral Express has distinguished itself time and again against the Destruction, and bears an irreplaceable duty for the future. I can't just sit idly and watch you face annihilation...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: *sigh* Give me a break. I really am terrible at all this diplomatic talk.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Mr. Sunday, what makes you think that everything I've done is just to save Planarcadia?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: What?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Weal is where Woe lurks. Woe is where Weal leans." The good fortune of some often births the ill fate of others, and a dead end for someone may hide an opportunity for another.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: This treacherous land where life and death turn again and again, where fortune flips to misfortune, is, in my eyes, the perfect board for a game of wits.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: A game with whom?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...With the gods.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Mr. Sunday, have you heard of the "Battle of the Fanghu" thirty years ago?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: My bat's been itching for some action!
Let's go!
Just leave it to me!
I've heard rumors of that war, but not the details. General, are you suggesting Planarcadia is now facing dangers just as perilous as the Xianzhou Fanghu was back then?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: There's no coercion involved anywhere in this. It's a simple "Yes" or "No," like scrolling to the bottom of the Terms of Service.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: You got that right.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Thirty years ago, the Abundance Axis broke our lines and invaded the Fanghu homeland. The abominations awakened a living demonic star, intending to sink the Xianzhou Fanghu.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: With no other options, the Alliance staked everything on my junior soror's plan... to operate the astronomical observation device, the Cloudpeer Telescope, to signal the Reignbow for aid, using THEIR Lux Arrow to strike down the demon star.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Whoever operated the Cloudpeer Telescope would not return. It was to be a one-way trip.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: So your junior soror...?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You guessed wrong. The one who offered his life was my master, who taught me divination. It was Master Jingtian, then the Yuque's Master Diviner, and the only high official authorized to operate that device. He accepted his fate and ventured to the Fanghu.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Meanwhile, somewhere in Duomension City...
Going with him into certain death were Yueyu, the previous Yaoqing General who guarded the Cloudpeer Telescope, and the Verdant Knights under her command.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I was responsible for assessing the entire plan's feasibility and mending its gaps. I activated the Deca-Light Reflection Barrier, calculating and casting lots again and again.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I watched as the "starlight" representing countless possibilities flickered within the reflections — faint, wavering — until the vast shadow of a pondering god swallowed them whole, and they vanished into the abyssal dark at the edges of the universe.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: In that moment, I understood that I had cemented my master and countless soldiers into an inescapable doom. When the Lux Arrow fell, they would perish along with the enemy and that demonic star... all reduced to ashes.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You sacrificed so many comrades just to ensure the enemy's fall?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: To Penaconians, that must seem incredibly cruel, right?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: ...As someone born in an era of peace, I have no right to judge. Perhaps the founders of Penacony could understand the necessity.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Cruel or not, it was my duty. And so I had to witness, and remember their sacrifice.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: When I saw the Lux Arrow descend, I realized the Xianzhou Alliance had actually directed an Aeon's actions.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: In that case, general, it's all the more reason for you to wear the mask. Once your sight into the future is strengthened, you won't need to fear the "deathly omen" in your readings.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This realization illuminated the mission of my remaining years. In this cold, merciless cosmos, when you're trapped in despair, an Aeon's intervention is often the only hope.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: We are not ants, helpless beneath the celestial spheres as we simply watch the {RUBY_B#Aeons}stars{RUBY_E#} turn. Instead, {RUBY_B#Paths}THEIR trails{RUBY_E#} were forged by us, who offered up a portion of our insignificant destiny.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Even beings as mighty as the Aeons can be pulled by our will!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: ...Is this what you want to do in Planarcadia?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But the moment I laid hands on the mask, I understood the consequences of wearing it. Once this miraculous item is donned, the "Eye of Īśvara" would transcend mere sight and permeate throughout this realm. The Kālacakra Skyplume would predict the future of all beings at tens of billions of instances per second.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Indeed. I will seize those "starlights of possibility" I once buried with my own hands. Just like the Battle of the Fanghu thirty years ago: an Arbiter-General will fall, and an Aeon will descend.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I will forge the destined death into wagers and game pieces, and invite {RUBY_B#Aha}the god who delights in meddling with destiny{RUBY_E#} to sit at my table.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: This time, I will invite THEM into my calculations... to draw a Great Weal for the cosmos's future!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Mr. Sunday, surely you can understand this mad idea of mine, having once reached the divine throne of {RUBY_B#Ena}Order{RUBY_E#} yourself?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Our common ground goes far beyond "mad ideas."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But I was reviving a god who already lay dead and buried in the infinite dark. General... how can you be sure that the most capricious Aeon would be led by your fancy?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Have you heard this myth about the Elation?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Mr. Sunday, answer me: why did Aha laugh?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I think it's because THEY finally saw an audience arrive at this long-empty stage we call the universe.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Well said! You're way funnier than you look!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: As divination teaches: "Heaven creates forty-nine paths. Humans find the one unseen." WE are the greatest variable this blind, mindless universe can produce.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Ah, looks like it's about time...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Don't tell me you're disappearing without a goodbye again, general?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: No. This time, we will set our eyes on the same place and carve a sliver of possibility out of destiny with our own "sight."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Yes. The crimson light there pierces the sky today, marking it as a locus of Woe. The arcadia's first calamity will erupt there.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Forget it. The stuff in those pouches is all harmless banter anyway... Let's spare them.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Hello everyone, welcome back to Fulwish TV's special news segment, Arcadian Morning Report! I'm your host, Poofy!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Hi everyone, I'm your host, Snowie!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: It's been three hours since our first Supplicant, Miss Sparxie, announced her entry into the Phantasmoon Games. The performance she announced to all her fans, SparxiCon, is also about to begin!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: How curious! Planarcadia's day–night cycle was completely scrambled in ancient times! Graphia Academy's location just happens to be bathed in light...
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: So, in broad daylight, what kind of fireworks show does Miss Sparxie have in store for us?
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Hey, senior, you can't joke about that! Dear viewers, our apologies! Let's move on to news about other Supplicants.
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: According to the Department of Aberration Defense's staff, during a routine inspection of the Phantasmoon Courtyard, two additional mask shapes manifested on the altar.
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: In other words, two more Supplicants have appeared!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Although none of them have publicly announced entry into the games yet, the altar's masks mean someone, somewhere, has quietly donned the "Masks of Elation."
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: As for the two masks, Department of Aberration Defense staff describe one as a raccoon and the other as some kind of bird...
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: A raccoon mask, huh... Hard not to think of the Astral Express that just arrived in Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Will the Nameless from the Astral Express join the Phantasmoon Games? I hear they were also invited to SparxiCon as special guests!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Hmm! Will it be a miraculous show formed out of the collaboration between Supplicants, or a head-to-head showcase between two famed contenders?
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Countless streamers are already live, broadcasting the scene at the venue, let's cut to the feed now...
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Ah! Look, it's the Nameless from the Astral Express!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Lady

rows.text: One girl, a thousand faces! A thousand faces, one girl! Welcome to the SparxiCon live broadcast!
rows.speaker: Broadcast

rows.text: Dear lovely fans, please be patient ♥! SparxiCon is about to begin!
rows.speaker: Broadcast

rows.text: This horror stream is about to end. Time for you all to log off.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: That woman has Miss Sparxie's face! What a pathetic imitation!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Lady

rows.text: What? My face is the original!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Miss Sparxie's face alone is the greatest masterpiece in the world!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Man

rows.text: Everyone should listen to her sweet voice and gaze upon her adorable face!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Man

rows.text: We shall become Miss Sparxie!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Lady

rows.text: We offer everything to Miss Sparxie~!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Man

rows.text: Sparxicle! Sparxicle! Sparxicle!
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Men and Women

rows.text: Ugh... my eyes! I've seen something cursed!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: The memetic virus spread among people is way worse than we imagined. There are walking Sparxie-shrooms growing on the ground... I bet we'll all end up with Sparxie... or rather, Sparkle faces before we can get very far.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Who knows? Maybe she'll blow the school sky-high in a blaze of fireworks? After all, at the Phantasmoon Games fifteen years ago, Graphia Academy also...
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Become a fake of a fake, or a carefree monkey. Your call.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: On second thought... being assimilated by an impostor doesn't sound that bad...
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Enough talk. Eyes on the banana.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Ow! ...Bana! Ma'am, a little warning before you stab someone with a banana, please!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Come on! Bana!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Remember the plan we made at the tavern?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yes bana! ...I mean, we dig out the imagenated painting Sparxie hid, then use "waves" to give Graphia Academy a good banana-over... I mean, wash-over!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: But... what if that impostor figures it out?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Just try to keep her busy and buy us some time.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's do it!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Drop the act, my dear mask. I shouldn't have called you an "impostor." That was harsh of me.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Come back to mama's arms. It's not too late. If the Astral Express crew gets involved, they won't be pulling any punches.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Of course, I get it. Surrendering now would ruin the stage you so carefully set. Total buzzkill, right?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Pfft, hahaha... So you still don't get it!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: "The worst thing an actor should do is be tied down to one type of role."
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Standing before you, the loyal friend who's been by your side all along, the Masked Fool who never played any tricks...
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: SHE is actually the old mask I have shed.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Haven't I been telling you all this time? She's just an OLD MODEL.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: No wonder the light orb in the tavern didn't react to Sparkle.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...For real!? That explanation is... kinda awesome!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Look at those expressions on your faces! This is the best opening act for SparxiCon ever!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: I shed that old mask, and with it, the weak, timid, all-too-human me.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: This new me will break free from all shackles, gather my fans' Wishpower, and stride onto the stage of the Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Isn't that exactly what they crave? Elation in three minutes flat?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Nameless, you're doomed to lose. You can't stop what people desire...
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: We can't stop their desire, but in this stream, we'll show this arcadia world another possibility.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What did you just say?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: We'll show everyone watching the livestream the Elation of the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You... got another mask!?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: "Before SparxiCon begins, the hero of the Express will defeat the villain who tried to spread the virus." And soon, the world will watch it happen live. In their hearts, they'll long for the Trailblaze too.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You were never the only option for the audience, Sparxie.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You know why I can't stand "heroic stories"? You lot always wave the flag of "justice," then stomp all over the fun with brute force.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: The Elation has nothing to do with justice! And you haven't won yet!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Ma'am! Gray Hair! Don't tell me you forgot the plan? I'll stall her.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: We don't have much time left, do we? I'm trying to give us better odds of winning here.
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: A long, long time. Come on, Gray Hair, have a little faith in me!
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: There's one thing I've always wondered: who's the real Sparkle, and who's just a mask... shouldn't the last one standing decide that?
rows.speaker: Sparkle

rows.text: Then let's settle it right now. I'll make you the opening firework of SparxiCon!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: AAAAAHHHHH...
rows.speaker: Sparkle & Sparxie

rows.text: Unbelievable! A girl who looks exactly like Miss Sparxie just rushed in and started throwing punches.
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Man

rows.text: Could she be... a high-grade lookalike rival?
rows.speaker: "Sparxified" Man

rows.text: March, I brought backup!
After [Trailblazer] escaped the school, I figured {M#he'd}{F#she'd} bring you back. So while Sparxie was away, I found a classroom to hide in.
rows.speaker: March 7th
